title: Consolidate app-wide layering into one canonical z-index scale (#178)
body:
Closes #178.

## What changed

Every app-wide z-index magic number now reads from one named scale,
`src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/layer/z_layers.js`. 15 raw literals → 1 documented
exemption (`public/index.html`, static boot-shell CSS that cannot import JS).

| tier | value | who |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTENT_RAISED` | 10 | local accents |
| `SCROLL_OVERLAY` | 500 | scrollbar thumb overlay |
| `APP_CHROME` | 1000 | title bar |
| `APP_CHROME_TOP` | 2000 | side menu |
| `MODAL` | 3000 | blocking dialogs |
| `TOAST` | 4000 | notifications |
| `TOOLTIP` | 5000 | tooltip, explorer label ghost |
| `POPOVER_BLOCKER` | 6000 | popover click-outside catcher |
| `POPOVER` | 7000 | context menu, color picker panel |
| `DRAG_GHOST` | 8000 | explorer drag ghost |
| `TOP_PROGRESS` | 9000 | global progress bar |
| `BOOT` | 2147483647 | boot overlay |

Each tier's position is justified in the module header by a real scenario, not
by taste, and each justification has a matching invariant test. The contract
test asserts *orderings*, so values can be retuned freely as long as every
scenario still holds.

## Three deviations from the issue text

**1. The issue's scale is missing tiers.** It puts everything above `MODAL`
into one `POPOVER` rank. PR #192 (already in `dev`) established, and
`explorer.test.js` regression-tests, `MODAL < TOOLTIP < POPOVER` — flattening
those would reintroduce the exact bug #192 fixed.

**2. The issue is stale on the explorer ghost.** It says the ghost is at
`999999` and should drop to `CONTENT_RAISED(10)`. On `dev` it is already
`10000`, deliberately: Explorer renders *inside* `memory_inspect_modal`,
`theme_editor`, and `recipe_list`, so pushing it below `MODAL` would let a
modal hide its own rows' hints.

**3. The issue's `TOAST > POPOVER` ordering is wrong** — see below.

## Landing spot: `BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/layer/`, not `SERVICEs/`

33 of the 62 z-index-bearing files live in `BUILTIN_COMPONENTs`, a layer that
today imports `SERVICEs` only for runtime behavior (buses, bridges), never for
constants. Adding ~10 primitives→services edges would turn it from a leaf into
something hanging off the system-access layer, and mini_ui — the upstream these
components were ported from — has zero such imports, so a component that gained
one could not be ported back.

The singular directory name matches mini_ui's `layer/`, which also holds a
`layer_stack.js` owning the *behavioral* dismiss stack (top layer, Escape,
outside-click). **PuPu has not ported that** — `modal.js:47`,
`context_menu.js:53`, and `tooltip.js:805` each wire their own Escape listener,
with no shared stack. The name reserves the spot; the docs record the debt.

## Bugs fixed on the way

- **toast tied with modal.** Both at `9999`, so which painted on top depended
  on portal insertion order. A save-confirmation toast landing behind the modal
  that triggered it is invisible UX breakage.
- **color picker's blocker tied with modal.** Same tie. Its own test is titled
  *"above a modal"* — intent documented, held by luck.
- **three files independently hardcoded `10000`.** Two meant "tooltip tier",
  the picker meant "interactive popover". They now say which.

## Two defects caught by adversarial review, after the first push

**`TOAST` was placed above `POPOVER`** (following the issue's ordering), which
silently reversed pre-migration behavior where context menu (99999) always beat
toast (9999). This is reachable in production: `toast.error()` from
`use_chat_stream` gets `Infinity` duration, and the toast pile sets
`pointerEvents:'auto'` across its whole bounding box deliberately. A lingering
error toast overlapping an open context menu eats the click, and the menu's
outside-mousedown handler reads that as an outside click and **silently closes
the menu instead of running the item**. Fixed: `TOAST < TOOLTIP < POPOVER`.

**The picker's blocker and panel were collapsed onto one value.** Before, panel
`10000` > blocker `9999`. `theme_editor` renders a column of ColorPickers with
no focus trap and the popover never takes focus, so Tab+Enter can open a
second; tied, the second instance's transparent full-viewport blocker paints
over the first's panel and closes the wrong picker. Fixed with
`POPOVER_BLOCKER`.

Review also caught a **false claim I had written in three places** (that
`layer_stack.js` already existed in PuPu — I had read mini_ui's copy while the
shell was still in that repo) and **two holes in the guard itself**: it scanned
line-by-line so `zIndex:\n  9999` slipped through, and it exempted itself
file-wide. Both fixed and re-verified by injection.

## Ordering audit

All 91 before/after pairs were compared exhaustively. 28 orderings change:
10 are the deliberate un-tying of modal/toast/blocker (all `9999`), 8 involve
`variable_picker` (dead code boxed inside `overflow:hidden`), and the rest are
intended semantic corrections. No unaccounted flips remain.

One deliberate new tie: picker panel and context menu are both `POPOVER`. An
open picker's blocker intercepts the right-click first, so they cannot coexist.

## Verification

- frontend **317 suites / 3147 tests** green (baseline before this branch:
  315 / 3127 — the delta is exactly this branch's new tests)
- electron **30 suites / 514 tests** green
- production webpack build succeeds; the scale appears in the bundle as
  `CONTENT_RAISED:10,SCROLL_OVERLAY:500,APP_CHROME:1e3,…` and every old magic
  number (9999/10000/99999/999999/2048/2049) is gone from the output
- guard verified to actually bite, twice: injecting `zIndex: 4242` and the
  split-across-lines `zIndex:\n 7777` both fail it with the exact file:line

## ⚠️ Still needs human eyes

Automated tests cannot see paint order. Before merging:

1. right-click a sidebar chat → hover a truncated title → **title stays under
   the menu**
2. open chat memory (memory-inspect modal) → hover a truncated row → **ghost
   appears above that modal** ← most at risk from this change
3. settings → appearance → open a color picker → **above the modal, clickable**
4. trigger a toast while a modal is open → **now above it** (intended change)
5. leave an error toast up, then open a context menu under it → **menu wins**
6. drag a chat/folder → ghost above content, reorder still commits
7. cold start → boot overlay covers everything
8. **scroll any long list and confirm the scrollbar thumb is visible** — this
   overlay dropped from 9999 to 500 and is used in 40 places

## Out of scope (recorded, not fixed)

- `dnd/context.js:90` — @dnd-kit's `DragOverlay` defaults to `999` with no
  `zIndex` pass-through in our wrapper, so a dragged item there can fall behind
  overlays. Needs a prop; deserves its own issue.
- `top_progress_bar` is mounted nowhere, so its constant has no observable
  effect. Restoring `<TopProgressBar />` is a product question.
- `variable_picker` needs a portal to work at all.
- Visual order and behavioral (dismiss) order are still two independent
  systems; see the debt note above.

## Unrelated commit in this branch

`da631d8d` carries CTO/architect review records for the codex
context-memory-v2 migration. They landed here because those agents were
dispatched from the same session and the main checkout has 209 uncommitted
paths nobody should touch. Drop it if you'd rather it go elsewhere.

title: fix(explorer): keep the truncated-label ghost under menus and dismiss it on press
body:
## 症状

Explorer 行标签被截断时,hover 会浮出显示完整标签的 ghost。它有两个独立缺陷:

1. 点开 modal 后不会消失,一直悬着
2. 会盖在 context menu 和 modal 前面

## 根因(两个症状 = 两个独立根因)

**层级**:ghost 写死 `zIndex: 999999`,比 modal(9999) 和 context menu(99999) 都高一个数量级。库内通用 `tooltip/tooltip.js` 用的是 10000,explorer 这个值是个离群魔数。

**生命周期**:`clearOverflow` 只挂在 mouseleave 和 scroll 上。点击行打开 modal 时指针仍停在该行,**mouseleave 永远不会触发**,所以 ghost 一直挂着。

## 修复

`zIndex: 999999` → `10000`。这个值两边都是刻意的:

- **高于 modal(9999)**:Explorer 会被用在 modal *内部*(`memory_inspect_modal.js`),压到 9999 以下会让 modal 遮住自己行的提示
- **低于 context menu(99999)**:ghost 是被动提示,绝不该盖住可交互菜单

`handleMouseDown` 里加 `clearOverflow()`,覆盖左键(开 modal)和右键(开菜单)。调用放在 `shouldSkipRowDragStart` 早返回**之前**——一旦按下,交互已开始,提示就该让位,哪怕这次按下不会启动拖拽。

未动 1949 行拖拽跟随 ghost 的 999999:拖拽与右键菜单互斥,且未报告该症状。

## 验证

先写测试见红(4 failed,报错直接打印出 `z-index: 999999`),再改实现。

- `explorer` 套件 **15/15** 通过,含 10 个原有用例(拖拽 ghost、trailing mousedown 不启动拖拽等未受影响)
- 消费方回归(side-menu / memory-inspect / theme_editor / recipes_page):**34 套件 / 187 测试**全绿

新增 5 个用例锁定两条契约,包括"在 600ms 延迟窗口内按下后,定时器到期也不得再冒出 ghost"这个边缘情况。

其中一条断言 `zIndex > 9999` 是**保护性**的——防止后来者把层级压得太低而破坏 modal 内的用法。

title: Establish a public API boundary between PuPu and unchain — remove private-module imports, monkey-patching, and undeclared attribute injection
body:
## What & Why

PuPu's Flask sidecar (`unchain_runtime/`) consumes `unchain`, a separate Python library living in its own repository, linked as an editable sibling install. Although the two are separate repos with separate licenses, PuPu currently reaches **past** unchain's public API in four distinct ways: it imports a private module, monkey-patches methods onto live unchain objects at runtime, injects 11 attributes onto unchain's `Agent` class that the class never declares, and imports from 14 deep submodule paths rather than the package root.

The consequence is a recurring breakage class the team has already named and paid for once: **kwarg drift**. When unchain changes an internal method signature or attribute, PuPu breaks silently — there is no contract to violate, so nothing catches it. Commit `4a9fd9c6` ("transparent contract proxy for unchain memory APIs — end the kwarg-drift breakage class") was a tactical fix for exactly one instance of this. This issue is the structural fix.

This work is a prerequisite for treating unchain as a versioned dependency rather than a same-tree edit. It is **not** about publishing unchain as a third-party-consumable library — that decision is explicitly out of scope (see Non-Goals).

## Read this first

| Document | Why |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` (repo root) | Project conventions, high-risk pitfalls, GitNexus workflow |
| `.claude/CLAUDE.md` | Architecture overview, request flow, IPC boundary |
| `docs/DEV_GUIDE.md` | Full documentation index — start here for the big picture |
| `docs/architecture/` | Request flow, memory, storage |

**Environment setup:**

```bash
npm start                                    # full dev (React :2907 + Electron)
cd unchain_runtime/server && python main.py  # Python backend standalone
npm test                                     # Jest
```

The `unchain` library must be present as a sibling checkout and installed editable. Confirm with `python -c "import unchain; print(unchain.__file__)"`.

## Architecture at a glance

```
React (use_chat_stream.js)
  -> IPC bridge -> Electron main
    -> HTTP/SSE -> Flask (unchain_runtime/server/)
      -> unchain library   <=== THIS BOUNDARY IS THE SUBJECT OF THIS ISSUE
        -> Provider SDK (OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Ollama)
```

`unchain_runtime/server/` is PuPu's own code. Everything it imports from `unchain.*` crosses a repository boundary. Today that boundary is porous in both directions: unchain changes internals without semver discipline, and PuPu patches internals rather than consuming a stable surface.

## The four violation classes (all verified in the current tree)

### Class 1 — Private module import (1 site)

| File:Line | Code |
|---|---|
| `unchain_runtime/server/main.py:15` | `from unchain.jobs._worker import main as worker_main` |

`_worker` is private by naming convention. PuPu spawns it as a subprocess entry point. unchain has no obligation to keep it stable.

### Class 2 — Monkey-patching unchain objects at runtime (3 patchers, `memory_factory.py`)

| Symbol | Line | What it patches |
|---|---|---|
| `_patch_qdrant_similarity_search_compat` | 1347 | Replaces `vector_adapter._client` with a compat wrapper |
| `_patch_memory_commit_with_overlap` | 1415 | Rebinds `manager.commit_messages` via `MethodType` |
| `_patch_memory_prepare_with_diagnostics` | 1527 | Rebinds `manager.prepare_messages` via `MethodType` |

Applied at `memory_factory.py:1723`, `1735`, `1807`, `1808`. Each guards re-entry with a `_pupu_*_patch` sentinel flag. `_preserve_bound_method_signature` (line 1313) exists **solely** to keep the patched signature aligned with unchain's — this helper is itself the clearest evidence that the boundary is being violated, and it is the mitigation that commit `4a9fd9c6` added.

Note the failure mode is loud-but-late: `_patch_memory_commit_with_overlap` raises `"memory commit overlap patch requires an inspectable commit_messages API"` if unchain's signature becomes uninspectable — a runtime error, not a build-time one.

### Class 3 — Injecting undeclared attributes onto `unchain.Agent` (11 attributes, 15 assignment sites)

`unchain_adapter.py:5448-5466` and `5972-5985` set:

```
_orchestration_role      _orchestration_mode     _orchestration_next_mode
_memory_runtime          _max_iterations         _toolkits
_display_model           _selected_model         _developer_model_id
_general_model_id        _max_context_window_tokens
```

**None of these are declared on unchain's `Agent` class** (verified against `src/unchain/agent/agent.py`). PuPu invents them, writes them, and reads them back at `unchain_adapter.py:5553`, `5554`, `6078`, `6157`, `6333`. unchain is unaware they exist — a future `__slots__`, a dataclass conversion, or a rename of the internal agent object breaks PuPu with no warning.

### Class 4 — Deep submodule imports (14 distinct paths)

```
10x  unchain.agent.modules            5x  unchain.tools.messages
 5x  unchain.memory.checkpoint_state  5x  unchain.interaction.runtime
 5x  unchain.interaction.durable      4x  unchain.kernel.types
 4x  unchain.kernel.lifecycle_events  2x  unchain.jobs._worker
 2x  unchain.agent.model_io           1x  each: unchain.tools.{toolkit,tool,receipts,models,confirmation}
```

unchain's `src/unchain/__init__.py` exports a narrow `__all__`; PuPu consumes ~14 paths beneath it. Not all of these are wrong — but none are currently *declared* as supported, so there is no way to tell which unchain is allowed to change.

## Suggested development path

Do these in order. Steps 1–2 are pure documentation/measurement and carry no runtime risk; land them first so later steps have a baseline.

**Step 1 — Build the three-tier API ledger.**
Create `docs/architecture/unchain-api-surface.md`. Enumerate every `unchain.*` symbol PuPu imports or touches, classified as:

- **stable-public** — safe to consume, unchain commits to it
- **adapter-supported** — consumed today, needs a shim, unchain may change with notice
- **internal-violation** — must be eliminated (all of Class 1–3 starts here)

Self-check: the ledger's import list must match `grep -rn "from unchain" unchain_runtime/ --include="*.py" | grep -v /tests/` exactly.

**Step 2 — Write characterization tests before changing anything.**
Add `unchain_runtime/server/tests/test_unchain_api_contract.py` asserting the *current* behavior of each violation site: that `Agent` accepts the 11 injected attributes, that `commit_messages`/`prepare_messages` have the signatures the patchers expect, that `unchain.jobs._worker.main` is importable and callable. These tests must **pass before and after** your refactor — they are the safety net, not the goal.

Self-check: `pytest unchain_runtime/server/tests/test_unchain_api_contract.py` green on an unmodified tree.

**Step 3 — Replace Class 3 (attribute injection) with an explicit side-table.**
Introduce a PuPu-owned `AgentRuntimeState` dataclass in a new `unchain_runtime/server/agent_runtime_state.py`, keyed by agent identity (e.g. a `WeakKeyDictionary` or an explicit id). Move all 11 attributes there. Update the 15 write sites and the 5 read sites.

This is the highest-value step: it removes PuPu's dependence on unchain's object internals entirely, and it is testable in isolation.

Self-check: `grep -c "agent\._" unchain_runtime/server/unchain_adapter.py` drops to 0 (excluding `_pupu_`-prefixed names).

**Step 4 — Replace Class 2 (monkey-patching) with composition.**
Wrap the memory manager in a PuPu-owned decorator object that *delegates* to unchain's manager rather than rebinding its methods. The overlap and diagnostics logic moves into the wrapper. `_preserve_bound_method_signature` should become deletable.

Self-check: `_patch_memory_*` functions gone; `memory_factory.py` no longer calls `MethodType`.

**Step 5 — Address Class 1 and Class 4 (imports).**
For `jobs._worker`: request a public entry point from unchain (e.g. `unchain.jobs.worker_main`) and consume that. For the deep imports: either promote the path to `stable-public` in the ledger, or route it through a thin `unchain_runtime/server/unchain_api.py` facade so there is exactly one place to fix when unchain moves things.

**Step 6 — Add a lint gate.**
An AST check or ruff rule in CI that fails on: any `from unchain.*._*` import, any `setattr` targeting an unchain-owned object, and any `MethodType` rebinding of an unchain method. Without this, the violations grow back.

## How to verify done

**Acceptance criteria:**

1. `docs/architecture/unchain-api-surface.md` exists and classifies every `unchain.*` consumption site into one of the three tiers, with zero entries left in `internal-violation`.
2. `grep -rn "from unchain\.[a-z_.]*\._" unchain_runtime/ --include="*.py" | grep -v /tests/` returns nothing.
3. `grep -o "agent\._[a-z_]*" unchain_runtime/server/unchain_adapter.py | grep -v _pupu_` returns nothing.
4. No `MethodType` rebinding of unchain methods remains in `memory_factory.py`.
5. The lint gate from Step 6 is wired into CI and fails a deliberately-introduced violation.

**Verification means:**

```bash
cd unchain_runtime/server && python -m pytest tests/ -v   # full backend suite
npm test                                                   # Jest (should be unaffected)
```

Plus an end-to-end smoke run via the `pupu-test-api` skill: send a chat message, confirm streaming works, confirm memory prepare/commit still fire, confirm a subagent run completes. The memory two-phase (`memory_prepare` / `memory_commit`) and subagent lifecycle events are the surfaces most likely to regress — check them explicitly in the frontend event stream.

## Impact / risk

**Blast radius (measured by direct grep over the current tree, not by call-graph analysis):**

| Surface | Sites | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `unchain_adapter.py` attribute injection | 15 writes + 5 reads | **HIGH** — sits inside the streaming main loop (lines 5448–6333) |
| `memory_factory.py` patchers | 3 patchers, 4 call sites | **HIGH** — memory prepare/commit is a two-phase protocol the frontend renders |
| `main.py` private import | 1 | MEDIUM — subprocess entry point; failure is at worker spawn |
| Deep imports | 14 paths / 16 files | LOW individually, MEDIUM in aggregate |

**HIGH RISK — read before starting.** Steps 3 and 4 touch code inside PuPu's live streaming path. `unchain_adapter.py:6390-7094` wraps every agent run in interject channel registration; the agent object and memory manager are live participants there. A regression here degrades chat streaming, memory persistence, or subagent orchestration — all user-visible.

Mitigations, in order of importance: (a) land Step 2's characterization tests first and keep them green throughout; (b) do Steps 3 and 4 as **separate** PRs, not one; (c) run the end-to-end smoke after each.

**Reversibility:** Steps 1, 2, 6 are purely additive and fully reversible. Steps 3–5 are behavior-preserving refactors — reversible, but only cheaply so if Step 2 landed first.

**Non-goals (explicitly out of scope):**

- Declaring unchain's API stable to third parties. unchain is currently PuPu's internal implementation; it has its own repo and license so that it *can* be opened later, but there is no commitment to do so. Any "announce stable API" work requires separate approval.
- Replacing unchain with an off-the-shelf harness. Ruled out by prior architectural adjudication.
- Pinning unchain to a released version. Related and complementary, but tracked separately.

title: Harden SQL migration and release durability
body:
## What changed

- Makes SQLite the durable authority for settings, chat state, provider credentials, toolkit preferences, computer-use preferences, token usage, and custom MCP icons while preserving safe legacy fallback during migration.
- Encrypts provider credentials through Electron `safeStorage`, removes secret-read IPC paths, serializes writes, and keeps rollback/retry behavior atomic.
- Handles missing or failing macOS Keychain storage with a session latch plus persisted retry cooldown, preventing repeated `PuPu Key` prompts and allowing legacy credential fallback.
- Adds coordinated renderer/main-process quit draining so pending settings, consent changes, local beta state, reset operations, chat drafts, and session bundles are durable before shutdown.
- Adds an idempotent guarded chat recovery journal so stale journal replay cannot overwrite newer SQLite state and quota/size failures synchronously fall back to SQL.
- Restricts the test API to E2E environments, hardens navigation/origin handling, and adds same-userData restart coverage.

## Why

The SQL migration had multiple release-blocking durability and security gaps: secrets could remain tied to legacy authority, Keychain failures retried on every boot, immediate quit could outrun async persistence, and a stale or oversized chat recovery journal could block shutdown or regress newer SQL data.

## User impact

- Existing users migrate without losing settings or chat state.
- Missing Keychain storage no longer causes repeated prompts every launch.
- Immediate quit/restart preserves pending drafts and settings mutations.
- Provider credentials remain encrypted at rest when Keychain storage is available and fail closed without exposing plaintext over IPC.

## Validation

- Deterministic release gate: PASS
- Frontend: 313 suites / 3,086 tests passed
- Electron: 152 suites / 1,468 tests passed
- Python backend: 963 tests passed, 3 skipped, 64 subtests passed
- MCP registry, production web build, license/notices, and Electron E2E smoke: PASS
- Full local fake-model soak: 21.1 minutes, 3 parallel root agents, 96 tool calls per agent, no page errors or forbidden log findings
- macOS arm64 unsigned DMG/ZIP build: PASS
- Packaged `.app` isolated launch/close smoke: PASS
- Security review: no remaining P0/P1 findings

## Release notes

The generated macOS artifacts are unsigned and not notarized. Real provider/Ollama/workspace smoke, Windows/Linux install checks, and the paid live-model matrix remain separate release steps.

title: feat(plugins): Computer Use moves into the plugins panel + per-plugin settings contract
body:
## Summary

Moves Computer Use configuration out of Settings and into the **plugins panel**, per CEO direction: capabilities all live in one place, and this establishes the **per-plugin settings page contract** that future toolkit customization (per-tool write confirmations, OAuth management, …) will reuse.

- **Installed → Built-in section** gains a synthetic "Computer" row (mouse icon, read-only On/Off status pill from server truth, always visible, participates in search). Not in the MCP catalog — same synthetic-entry precedent as the chat attach menu; backend untouched.
- **Row click opens a detail overlay** (existing `openDetail` mechanism, new `plugin_settings` kind) hosting the exact same `ComputerUseSettings` component — toggle, one-time consent, macOS permission badges. **UI moved, vessels untouched**: `settings/computer_use/` directory has zero changes; `enable_controller` remains the renderer's single call site (grep-test still passes unmodified).
- **New `plugin_settings_registry.js`** — the generic contract: `toolkitId → {Component, labelKey, icon}`. One entry today (`builtin.computer`); MCP per-tool permission panels register here later (exact-id keys now, `source:` fallback reserved as a future extension).
- **Settings nav entry removed** (added in #184; this supersedes it). All 11 locales updated both ways (nav key removed, plugin name/tagline added).

### Trust partition

Computer sits in the Built-in section with the builtin badge, physically separated from third-party MCP entries; its detail page renders **no TRUST_CONFIG vocabulary** (verified/community/needs_review is store trust language) and no install/delete/approve affordances.

## Summary

Adds the **user-writable enable path** for Computer Use (Gate B slice): a settings toggle that — after a one-time informed-consent gate — turns the computer-use tool on/off at runtime, no sidecar restart required.

Until now the feature flag (`PUPU_COMPUTER_USE`) was env-var only (dev-side, Gate A). This PR wires the full user path:

```
settings toggle → requireComputerUseConsent() → computer_use_enabled_store (localStorage, versioned)
  → window.unchainAPI.setComputerUseEnabled → IPC "unchain:set-computer-use-enabled"
    → electron main → authorized POST /computer-use/config (loopback + x-unchain-auth)
      → sidecar runtime override → mounted on the next chat request
```

**Note: this exposes the toggle in dev builds only in practice — the user-facing release is still blocked** until the screenshot-injection A/B eval passes and security gives the final Gate B release sign-off (tracked separately).

## Design decisions (pupu-architect, CTO signed off)

- **Runtime override as primary, spawn env as belt-and-braces**: electron main caches the desired state, re-pushes after sidecar crash-restart, and mirrors it into `PUPU_COMPUTER_USE` on respawn. No restart, no stream interruption; user's explicit OFF beats a dev env ON.
- **Red line preserved**: the mount funnel's flag gate never reads request options — the flag stays server-side authority (renderer-compromise cannot widen it).
- **Flag copies converged**: `unchain_adapter` and `memory_factory` (screenshot sanitization) now delegate to a single `computer_use_flag` leaf module — the tool gate and transcript hygiene can no longer drift apart.
- **Fail-closed everywhere**: cold start, crash-restart window, corrupted localStorage record, version mismatch, failed re-push — worst case is always "stays off".
- **Consent invariants**: decline → zero writes, zero pushes; boot re-sync re-validates consent before pushing true; renderer has a single `setComputerUseEnabled` call site, enforced by a grep-style test.

## Slices

| Slice | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | dev-backend | `computer_use_flag.py` leaf module, converged private copies, `POST /computer-use/config` (strict `{enabled: <bool>}`, 401/400 hardened) |
| B2 | dev-electron | IPC channel + parity manifests, main service (POST, tri-state desired cache, ready re-push, spawn env), preload boundary tightening |
| B3 | dev-settings | `computer_use_enabled_store` (anti-corruption reads), bridge facade, settings toggle (server-truth display state, pending/failure states), headless boot-sync host |

Plus one post-e2e fix: `setComputerUseEnabled` now returns `ok:true` (dead `ok` contract found by QA).

- Backend: **853 passed / 3 skipped** (+20 new; flag priority, endpoint hardening, sanitize-follows-flag)
- Electron: **121 passed** (+8 new; strict boolean, crash-restart re-push, cache-null no-op)

All PASS: fail-closed baseline → real-vessel enable (renderer→IPC→main→POST, no curl forgery) → funnel mount + claude-sonnet-4-6 screenshot round-trip (model accurately described the live screen) → on-disk transcript contains zero raw base64 (media_id references only) → disable takes effect next message → `kill -9` sidecar → auto-respawn restores enabled state without renderer involvement.

Adds **Computer Use (M2)** to PuPu: a built-in first-class tool that lets a capable Anthropic model control the user's real desktop — screenshots + mouse/keyboard injection — through PuPu's existing tool pipeline. GUI screen control only (browser automation was the deferred M1); Anthropic-first.

## What's in here

**Sidecar "hand" (`unchain_runtime/server/computer_control/`)** — new self-contained module: `mss` screenshot + downscale + coordinate/scale-map (Retina DPR=2 handled), `pynput` injection backends (macOS CGEvent / Windows SendInput / Linux X11 XTest), platform capability probing with Wayland degrade-to-screenshot-only.

Mount requires **all three**: flag on AND model-capable AND not a subagent run.

**Security (SEC-001 gate-B items, all code-complete):**
- **F1** — injection actions (click/type/key/scroll/drag/move) forced through server-side confirmation; read-only actions (screenshot/wait/cursor_position) exempt via fail-closed allowlist.
- **F9** — computer tool never mounted in recipe-subagent runs (no confirmation channel there).
- **F2** — screenshot prompt-injection: system-prompt security warning injected only when the computer tool is mounted; structurally zero-pollution for non-computer sessions.
- **F2 consent** — one-time informed-consent modal (reuses existing `AgreementModal`, no new panel), own localStorage key, versioned.
- **F3** — screenshot base64 stripped from on-disk session transcript (wraps `JsonFileSessionStore`; deep-walks messages + checkpoint; base64 → media reference, TTL-bounded).
- **F6** — pynput LGPL-3.0 written source-offer added to third-party notices generator + release gate for future copyleft deps.

**Media + status** — `GET /chat/tool-media/<id>` (TTL, loopback + token + unguessable id), `GET /computer-use/status` (capabilities + permissions for the settings panel).

**Frontend** — read-only settings panel (Screen Recording / Accessibility badges + system-settings deep links via main-process allowlist), status bridge, consent modal. Dev-visible only.

## Dependencies

Requires the unchain library changes **already merged to unchain `dev` (`52854bd`)**: S0 rich tool result (image blocks reach the model) + S1 provider-native predefined tools. The shipped sidecar must resolve an unchain build that contains S0/S1, or the computer tool will not function (it degrades: flag-off = inert, so no breakage on `dev` today).

- unchain S0/S1: 855 passed / 0 regression (dual-signed: llm-expert + CTO).
- sidecar server suite incl. all computer-control tests: 591 passed / 2 skipped / 0 regression.
- frontend: 1392 passed (consent store + modal + panel).

- **Wayland**: injection is second-phase (degrades to screenshot-only + explicit "not supported").
- **Overlay cursor visualization**: fast-follow after F1 baseline (feasibility spiked; screenshot-feedback-pollution risk retired via `setContentProtection`).

Branch is based on the older `dev@1d43c44`; `dev` has since advanced ~73 commits. Overlapping files (`unchain_adapter.py`, `routes.py`, `memory_factory.py`, IPC channels, `locales/en.json`) will need conflict resolution before merge — the diff itself is confined to the computer-use slice.

title: Consolidate app settings persistence into a main-process SQLite authority
body: ## What & Why PuPu's durable application settings are currently owned by the renderer and stored in one shared localStorage["settings"] JSON object. Several independent modules follow the same pattern: 1. Read the entire settings object. 2. Modify one nested section. 3. Serialize and write the entire object back. 4. Silently ignore parse or quota errors. This affects appearance and theme configuration, workspace selection, Memory configuration, feature flags, initial setup state, UI state, and development settings. The current arrangement creates several structural problems: - There is no single storage authority or schema migration layer. - Independent read-modify-write operations can overwrite unrelated sections with stale copies. - Persistence errors are usually swallowed, so the UI may appear to save a setting that is lost after restart. - Durable application state is tied to Chromium storage and the current renderer origin. - Startup consumers read storage through different helpers—and sometimes directly—so migration and validation behavior is inconsistent. - Theme state is split between renderer localStorage and the main-process theme-prefs.json. - Tests must mock browser storage even when testing application-level persistence behavior. Chat persistence has already established the intended architecture: main-process SQLite authority, a narrow preload bridge, a renderer-side memory mirror, transactional migration, and a pure-web/localStorage fallback. This ticket applies the same ownership model to non-sensitive application settings. ### In scope Move these settings into main-process SQLite: - appearance - theme mode - locale - theme preset - custom semantic colors - related appearance preferences - runtime - primary workspace root - workspace list and metadata - memory - enabled state - embedding provider/model selection - recall limits and thresholds - long-term Memory configuration - feature_flags - app - initial setup completion state - ui - persisted app-level UI preferences such as side-menu state - dev - development-only settings currently stored under the same root ### Explicitly out of scope - Chat data—already owned by userData/chats.db. - Memory contents: session transcripts, long-term profiles, character Memory, and Qdrant collections. - Provider API keys currently present under settings.model_providers. - MCP secrets, OAuth tokens, and OAuth app credentials. - Token-usage history. - Default toolkit selection and auto-approval state. - Agent-folder state and custom MCP icons. - Attachments, avatars, Recipes, Subagent files, downloaded runtimes, packages, and caches. - Auto-update preference unless required by the final storage-service initialization order. Secrets must not be copied into a plaintext SQLite database as part of this migration. Moving provider credentials into OS-backed secure storage requires a separate security-reviewed ticket. ## Read this first - CLAUDE.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md—project conventions. - AGENTS.md—GitNexus impact-analysis and change-detection requirements. - docs/DEV_GUIDE.md—documentation index. - docs/architecture/—Electron, preload, IPC, and storage boundaries. - docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-10-chat-storage-sqlite-main-authority.md—reference architecture for main-process SQLite authority and legacy migration. Critical constraints: - JavaScript only—no TypeScript or PropTypes. - React must not access ipcRenderer directly. - All system access goes through a narrow preload bridge. - IPC channel constants must match between shared, preload, and main-process registrations. - Keep .js and .cjs Electron tests in sync where both variants exist. - Run GitNexus impact analysis before changing any function, class, or method. - Do not modify Python Memory persistence in this ticket. Start the app with npm start. React-only development uses npm run start:web. Frontend tests use npm run test:frontend; Electron tests use npm run test:electron. ## Architecture at a glance ### Current ownership The renderer is the persistence authority: ~~~text React consumer -> localStorage.getItem("settings") -> parse whole root -> modify one section -> stringify whole root -> localStorage.setItem("settings") ~~~ The same root is accessed through multiple independent implementations: - ConfigContainer loads and saves startup/UI/appearance state. - Appearance storage manages theme preset and custom colors. - Runtime settings and initial setup both manage workspace state. - Memory settings manage runtime Memory options. - Feature flags manage persisted development overrides. - api.unchain.js reads runtime and provider settings again when preparing requests. Theme startup has an additional main-process copy in theme-prefs.json so the loading window and native theme can be selected before React renders. ### Desired ownership The Electron main process becomes the only durable authority: ~~~text React consumer -> canonical settings service and in-memory snapshot -> narrow window.appSettingsAPI bridge -> Electron main settings service -> userData/app.db ~~~ Reads needed during startup use one synchronous bootstrap snapshot, following the established chat-storage pattern. Normal writes update the renderer memory mirror immediately and send small section-level patches to the main process. Pure-web builds and jsdom tests retain a localStorage fallback behind the same renderer service API. Consumers must not know which backend is active. The Python sidecar does not open or write app.db. ## Proposed database boundary Create a separate userData/app.db. Do not add settings tables to chats.db; chat data and application configuration have different backup, migration, and lifecycle boundaries. All SQLite calls must remain behind one thin adapter so the experimental node:sqlite dependency can be replaced without changing consumers. Suggested initial schema: ~~~sql CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_meta ( key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL ); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_settings ( section TEXT PRIMARY KEY, payload TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL ); ~~~ Initial section names: ~~~text appearance runtime memory feature_flags app ui dev ~~~ Each payload is normalized JSON for one section. A section-level row keeps the first migration small while preventing unrelated settings from overwriting one another. Store a schema version in app_meta. Future schema changes must use explicit, ordered migrations and must never silently reset unreadable data to defaults. ## Relevant files | File | Current responsibility / expected change | |---|---| | src/CONTAINERs/config/container.js | Reads and writes the shared settings root during module initialization and runtime. Must bootstrap through the canonical settings service without introducing theme/UI flash. | | src/COMPONENTs/settings/appearance/storage.js | Owns theme preset and custom semantic color persistence. Migrate to the canonical service. | | src/COMPONENTs/settings/runtime.js | Owns workspace root and workspace-list persistence. Migrate to the canonical service. | | src/COMPONENTs/init-setup/steps/workspace.js | Contains a second direct workspace localStorage implementation. Remove the duplicate authority. | | src/COMPONENTs/init-setup/init_setup_storage.js | Persists app.setup_completed. Route through the canonical service. | | src/COMPONENTs/settings/memory/storage.js | Persists and normalizes Memory configuration. Preserve the existing normalized public shape. | | src/SERVICEs/feature_flags.js | Persists feature-flag overrides and publishes change notifications. Preserve build-default and production behavior. | | src/SERVICEs/api.unchain.js | Reads runtime, Memory, and provider settings while preparing requests. Replace in-scope direct reads; do not migrate provider credentials in this ticket. | | src/COMPONENTs/settings/dev/storage.js | Persists development-only settings under the shared root. | | src/COMPONENTs/settings/local_storage/index.js | Displays and clears browser storage. Update reporting so migrated settings do not appear lost or remain incorrectly deletable. | | electron/main/window/main_window.js | Reads/writes theme-prefs.json. Consolidate in-scope theme state into the new main-process settings authority. | | electron/main/services/chat_storage/db.js | Reference for the thin node:sqlite adapter pattern; do not couple settings to the chat schema. | | electron/main/services/chat_storage/service.js | Reference for WAL, transactions, initialization, migration, and close lifecycle. | | electron/shared/channels.js | Add the settings-storage IPC contract. | | electron/preload/channels.js | Register the allowed settings channels. | | electron/preload/index.js | Expose the narrow window.appSettingsAPI bridge. | | electron/main/ipc/register_handlers.js | Register synchronous bootstrap/import and asynchronous patch handlers. | | electron/main/index.js | Initialize and close the settings service in the correct application lifecycle order. | ## Suggested development path 1. **Freeze and normalize the data contract.** Create one renderer-level settings module, for example: ~~~text src/SERVICEs/settings_storage/ settings_storage_backend.js settings_storage_store.js settings_storage_schema.js ~~~ Define normalizers and defaults for every in-scope section. Preserve the public return shapes of the current feature-specific storage helpers so UI consumers do not require broad rewrites. Do not accept or persist model_providers, API keys, OAuth values, MCP secrets, or unknown credential-shaped fields. 2. **Create the main-process database service.** Add a small service under: ~~~text electron/main/services/app_settings/ ~~~ It should: - open userData/app.db; - enable WAL; - create and migrate the schema transactionally; - return the complete in-scope bootstrap snapshot; - import legacy settings once; - apply section-level patches transactionally; - close during application shutdown; - fail without deleting or replacing the existing database. 3. **Define a narrow IPC contract.** Proposed channels: | Channel | Mode | Purpose | |---|---|---| | BOOTSTRAP_READ | sendSync | Return the normalized settings snapshot before React initialization. | | IMPORT_LEGACY | sendSync | Transactionally import selected legacy localStorage sections and return success/failure. | | APPLY_PATCHES | send | Apply one or more section-level patches in one transaction. | The bridge must expose specific methods rather than a generic SQL, file, or arbitrary key-value API. 4. **Implement idempotent localStorage migration.** On first startup with an empty settings database: - Read the existing renderer settings root. - Select and normalize only the in-scope sections. - Exclude model_providers and all credential-bearing values. - Import the selected snapshot through IMPORT_LEGACY. - Mark migration complete only after the main process confirms the transaction. - If import fails, continue using the untouched localStorage source and retry next startup. - If the database already contains settings, it always wins over legacy localStorage. Keep the legacy localStorage value untouched for the initial release as a downgrade backup, but stop updating its migrated sections. Cleanup of the stale backup should be a later, explicit migration. 5. **Replace direct settings reads and writes.** Route all in-scope consumers through the canonical service: - ConfigContainer - Appearance/theme storage - Runtime/workspace storage - Initial setup - Memory settings - Feature flags - Development settings - Request preparation in api.unchain.js Add a guard test that prevents new production code from directly calling localStorage.getItem("settings") or localStorage.setItem("settings", ...). Exceptions should be limited to the migration/fallback backend and clearly documented. 6. **Preserve startup theme behavior.** Theme mode and background must be available before the main window becomes visible. Replace theme-prefs.json with reads from the new main-process settings service, and ensure the service initializes before main-window creation. The loading screen, native theme, React theme, and custom semantic colors must all resolve from the same persisted appearance section. Avoid adding a renderer round trip to determine the initial native theme. 7. **Preserve feature-flag semantics.** Development builds may continue to use persisted overrides. Production builds must continue to resolve flags from build-time defaults and ignore persisted development overrides. Existing subscriptions and syncBuildFeatureFlagsSnapshot behavior must remain intact. 8. **Preserve the pure-web/test fallback.** When window.appSettingsAPI is unavailable: - use localStorage through the same canonical backend; - preserve synchronous reads required during module initialization; - keep existing jsdom and React-only behavior; - avoid exposing backend-specific logic to feature consumers. 9. **Add migration and lifecycle tests.** Cover: - empty first launch; - migration from a complete legacy settings root; - migration with malformed or partial sections; - preservation of excluded model_providers; - idempotent repeated startup; - failed import followed by successful retry; - section patches not overwriting unrelated sections; - restart persistence; - database-open/schema failure without destructive reset; - pure-web fallback; - app shutdown and clean database close. Keep Electron .js and .cjs test variants aligned where required. ## How to verify done ### Acceptance criteria 1. An existing installation migrates appearance, workspace, Memory configuration, feature flags, setup state, UI state, and development settings without user-visible changes. 2. Every migrated value survives a full Electron restart. 3. Changing one settings section cannot overwrite another section. 4. Theme mode, loading background, native theme, locale, preset, and custom colors are correct on the first rendered frame—no light/dark flash. 5. Workspace root and workspace list continue to appear in Settings and are included in runtime request configuration exactly as before. 6. Memory settings produce the same normalized runtime payload as before migration. 7. Development feature-flag overrides persist; production builds still ignore persisted overrides and use build defaults. 8. Initial setup does not reappear after migration. 9. settings.model_providers and all provider credentials are not copied into app.db, logged, or exposed through the new settings bridge. 10. Production consumers no longer directly read or write localStorage["settings"]; only the migration/fallback backend may do so. 11. The Local Storage settings page accurately explains or displays the new settings database ownership. 12. A failed migration leaves legacy data untouched and retries safely on the next launch. 13. chats.db, Memory data, MCP data, attachments, and user-editable Recipe/Subagent files are unchanged. ### Automated verification - npm run test:frontend - npm run test:electron - Targeted tests for: - config container - appearance storage and theme editor - runtime/workspace settings - Memory settings and request payload injection - feature flags - initial setup storage - settings migration and database service - npm run build:web - git diff --check - GitNexus detect_changes({scope: "compare", base_ref: "main"}) before handoff ### Manual checkpoints 1. Start from a profile containing legacy localStorage settings. 2. Record theme, locale, workspace, Memory, and feature-flag values. 3. Launch the migrated build and confirm every value is unchanged. 4. Change each category independently and restart after each change. 5. Confirm the loading window and first React frame use the correct theme. 6. Confirm workspace selection still reaches a real chat request. 7. Confirm Memory settings still reach the sidecar with the same normalized values. 8. Launch a production build and confirm persisted development flags cannot override build defaults. 9. Temporarily make the database unavailable and confirm PuPu does not overwrite existing data with defaults. ## Impact / risk - **Risk: MEDIUM-HIGH.** The stored payloads are small, but the affected paths are load-bearing: application startup, initial theme selection, workspace routing, Memory request construction, and feature gating. - The largest correctness risk is initialization order. ConfigContainer currently reads settings during module evaluation, so the bootstrap snapshot must be synchronously available before those consumers initialize. - The largest migration risk is that sensitive model_providers data shares the same legacy root. Import must select explicit allowed sections rather than copying the entire settings object. - Theme currently has two persistence paths. Removing only one produces mismatched loading-window and React themes; both must converge on the same main-process authority. - Feature flags have different development and production semantics. Persisting them successfully must not make production flags user-overridable. - SQLite does not make credentials secure. Do not broaden this ticket into API-key or OAuth migration without security review. - node:sqlite remains experimental. Keep all engine-specific calls behind one adapter and avoid leaking database primitives into IPC or renderer code. - No Python sidecar persistence format should change. Electron must be restarted for main-process changes to take effect. - Roll out the migration behind an internal feature flag or staged build first, and retain the untouched legacy localStorage snapshot for at least one release to support downgrade.

title: Consolidate the app-wide layering (z-index) system into a single canonical scale
body: ## What & Why PuPu has no central z-index system. Every overlay component (modal, context menu, tooltip, toast, drag ghost, color picker, progress bar) invents its own magic number, and those numbers are not ordered by any shared rule. The result is stacking bugs where the wrong layer wins. The most visible symptom: when you right-click a chat in the sidebar and a context menu opens, hovering a truncated chat row makes its **full title + timestamp ("1w") paint on top of the context menu** — and the same overlay also paints on top of modals. This is because the sidebar's hover "full-label" overlay is portaled to `document.body` at `zIndex: 999999`, higher than the context menu (`99999`) and the modal (`9999`). We want one canonical, named layer scale (a single source of truth) that every overlay reads from, so layering is intentional and bugs like this become structurally impossible. ## Read this first - `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — project conventions. **Critical constraints**: JavaScript only (no TypeScript, no PropTypes), **inline styles only** (no CSS modules / styled-components), all function components. - `docs/DEV_GUIDE.md` — doc index. Then `docs/architecture/` (IPC boundary, storage) and `docs/conventions/styling.md` for the inline-style + `isDark` pattern. - Start the app: `npm start` (React on :2907 + Electron). React-only: `npm run start:web`. Tests: `npm test`. ## Architecture at a glance Relevant slice: **how overlays escape their parents**. Two mounting styles coexist and this matters for z-index: - **App-tree overlays** — rendered inline where they're declared; their z-index only competes *within their local stacking context* (e.g. `side_menu` container at `zIndex: 2049`, explorer drop indicators at `10/11`). - **Body-portal overlays** — `ReactDOM.createPortal(..., document.body)`, escaping all parent stacking contexts to compete directly at the body level. `modal`, `context_menu`, and the explorer hover/drag ghosts all do this. **These are the ones whose raw z-index values fight each other**, so their numbers must be globally ordered. The bug lives entirely in the body-portal tier: everything there is `position: fixed`/portaled, so the largest z-index wins outright. ## Relevant files | File | z-index today | What it is / why you'll touch it | |---|---|---| | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/explorer/explorer.js:977` | `999999` | **The bug.** `showFull` full-label ghost — portal to body, `position: fixed`. Must drop below the overlay tier. | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/explorer/explorer.js:1870` | `999999` | Drag ghost (follows cursor). Legitimately needs to be near-top, but should read a named token, not a literal. | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/context_menu/context_menu.js:120` | `99999` | Context menu, portal to body. Must sit above modals (so menus opened *from* a modal work). | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/modal/modal.js:61` | `9999` | Modal overlay, portal to body. | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/toast/toast_host.js:349` | `9999` | Toasts, portal. Currently ties with modal — undefined ordering. Should be above modals. | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/tooltip/tooltip.js:1081` | `10000` | Tooltip, portal. Above modal but below context menu today — inconsistent. | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/top_progress_bar/top_progress_bar.js:41` | `10000` | Global progress bar — should always be topmost. | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/color_picker/color_picker.js:704,717` | `9999/10000` | Popover color picker. | | `src/COMPONENTs/side-menu/side_menu.js:521` | `2049` | Sidebar container (app-tree, not a body portal). | | `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/class/scrollable.js:153` | `9999` | Scroll affordance. | (A full grep — `grep -rn "zIndex" src/ --include="*.js" | grep -v test` — returns ~151 hits; most are small local values like `0/1/2` that are fine. Only the body-portal / high-value ones above need to join the scale.) ## Suggested development path 1. **Create the single source of truth.** Add `src/SERVICEs/z_layers.js` (plain JS object, no TS) exporting named tiers in ascending order. Proposed scale — tune during review: ```js export const Z = { CONTENT_RAISED: 10, // in-flow accents: drop indicators, hover full-label ghost APP_CHROME: 100, // sidebar, sticky headers MODAL: 1000, // blocking dialogs POPOVER: 2000, // context menu / dropdown / tooltip / color picker (above modal, so menus from a modal work) TOAST: 3000, // notifications — above modals DRAG_GHOST: 4000, // follows cursor, above content overlays TOP_PROGRESS: 5000, // global progress bar — always topmost }; ``` Decide and **document the ordering rationale** in a header comment (what must sit above what, and why). 2. **Fix the reported bug first** (smallest, highest-value change): change `explorer.js:977` hover ghost from `999999` -> `Z.CONTENT_RAISED`. It's a reveal of existing row content and must never cover an overlay. Self-check: right-click a chat -> open context menu -> hover a long chat title; the title must stay *under* the menu. Repeat with a modal open. 3. **Migrate the body-portal overlays** to named tokens: `modal` -> `Z.MODAL`, `context_menu` -> `Z.POPOVER`, `tooltip` -> `Z.POPOVER`, `toast_host` -> `Z.TOAST`, explorer drag ghost -> `Z.DRAG_GHOST`, `top_progress_bar` -> `Z.TOP_PROGRESS`, `color_picker` popover -> `Z.POPOVER`. Verify each surface visually after each edit. 4. **Migrate app-tree containers** where they matter (`side_menu` -> `Z.APP_CHROME`, explorer drop indicators -> `Z.CONTENT_RAISED`). Leave trivially-local `0/1/2` values alone. 5. **(Optional, recommended) Add a guard test** in the spirit of the existing `shell_background_guard` test: assert no source file outside `z_layers.js` uses a raw z-index >= 1000, so the scale can't erode. Co-locate `.js`/`.cjs` variants if the electron test convention requires it. ## How to verify done - **Acceptance criteria:** 1. Right-click a sidebar chat -> context menu open -> hover any truncated chat title: the full title + "1w" stays **below** the context menu. 2. With a modal open, the sidebar hover ghost and any tooltip stay **below** the modal; a context menu / dropdown opened from inside the modal stays **above** it. 3. A toast appears **above** an open modal. 4. Drag ghost (dragging a chat/folder) rides above content but the reorder still works. 5. No overlay component contains a raw z-index literal >= 1000; all read from `z_layers.js`. - **Means:** `npm test` green (plus the new guard test if added). Manual checkpoints above in `npm start`. Optional smoke run via the `pupu-test-api` skill to confirm chat lifecycle still works after touching the sidebar/explorer. ## Impact / risk - **Risk: LOW-MEDIUM.** Changes are almost entirely style-value swaps with no logic change. Blast radius is wide (many UI surfaces) but shallow (each edit is one number). - The one behavior-changing edit is intentional: the explorer hover ghost drops from top-most to content tier — that *is* the fix, verify it doesn't now hide behind unexpected siblings within the sidebar. - `context_menu`, `modal`, `tooltip`, `toast` are shared primitives used across many screens — re-verify a sampling of surfaces (settings modal, toolkit modal, chat) after migrating them, not just the sidebar. - No IPC / Flask / storage surfaces touched.

title: Add Context7 to the MCP store registry (good first issue: register a new MCP server)
body:
### What & Why
PuPu ships an MCP toolkit **store** — a curated catalog of external MCP servers a user can install in one click. This ticket adds one new entry: **Context7** (`@upstash/context7-mcp`), an MCP server that fetches up-to-date official docs for libraries/frameworks so an agent stops hallucinating stale APIs. It's a deliberately ideal *first* ticket: the entire change is **one JSON file**, guarded by a schema, a one-command validator, and CI — you never touch the React ↔ IPC ↔ Flask install machinery, you just add data the existing pipeline already consumes. Along the way you learn how PuPu's toolkit store is wired.

### Read this first
- `docs/contributing/mcp-store-submission.md` — the contributor guide for exactly this task (copy-paste process + the human security-review gate).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/submit-mcp-server.yml` — the fields a store submission is expected to carry.
- `src/SERVICEs/mcp_toolkit_registry.json` — **the file you edit.** Skim a few existing entries; `memory.memory` is the closest template (stdio, npx, no OAuth).
- `src/SERVICEs/mcp_toolkit_registry.schema.json` — the JSON schema every entry must satisfy.
- Context7 upstream (verify all concrete values against these, don't trust this issue blindly): repo `https://github.com/upstash/context7`, npm `@upstash/context7-mcp`.

### Architecture at a glance
`mcp_toolkit_registry.json` is the single source of truth read by **both** the frontend (`src/SERVICEs/mcp_toolkit_store.js`) and the backend (`unchain_runtime/server/mcp_registry.py` resolves to the same file). The store page renders each entry as a card; no per-entry code exists — adding a server is purely appending one object to the `entries[]` array. `npm run validate:mcp` enforces the schema **plus** PuPu invariants a schema can't express (`toolkitId` must match `^mcp\.<server>\.<slug>$`, `id`/`toolkitId` globally unique, `category` must be one already declared in `registry.categories`, valid `trustLevel`).

### Relevant files
- `src/SERVICEs/mcp_toolkit_registry.json` — **the only file to change.** Add one object to `entries[]`.
- `src/SERVICEs/mcp_toolkit_registry.schema.json` — reference; tells you required vs optional fields (`entry` requires `id, toolkitId, name, description, mcp`; a `secret` supports `optional: true`).
- `scripts/validate-mcp-registry.cjs` (`npm run validate:mcp`, wired in `package.json`) — the validator you must pass; CI runs it too (`.github/workflows/validate-mcp-registry.yml`).
- `src/SERVICEs/mcp_toolkit_store.js` / `src/COMPONENTs/toolkit/pages/toolkit_store_page.js` — no change; read to see how your entry becomes a store card.

### Suggested development path
1. Copy the `memory.memory` entry as a starting shape, then adapt it. A minimal, review-safe skeleton (**verify every value against the Context7 README before filing — package version, tool names, and flags can drift**):
   ```json
   {
     "id": "dev.context7",
     "toolkitId": "mcp.dev.context7",
     "name": "Context7",
     "description": "Up-to-date, version-specific library docs and code examples for LLMs, fetched on demand.",
     "category": "dev",
     "source": "mcp",
     "trustLevel": "needs_review",
     "status": "available",
     "installable": true,
     "license": "MIT",
     "sourceRepo": "https://github.com/upstash/context7",
     "docsUrl": "https://github.com/upstash/context7",
     "mcp": {
       "transport": "stdio",
       "command": "npx",
       "args": ["-y", "@upstash/context7-mcp@<PIN_A_REAL_VERSION>"]
     },
     "setupPreview": "npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp",
     "prerequisites": ["Node.js >= 18"],
     "secrets": [
       { "key": "CONTEXT7_API_KEY", "label": "Context7 API key (optional, higher rate limits)", "optional": true }
     ],
     "tools": [
       { "name": "resolve-library-id", "title": "Resolve library ID", "requiresConfirmation": false },
       { "name": "get-library-docs", "title": "Get library docs", "requiresConfirmation": false }
     ],
     "readmeMarkdown": "## Context7\n\nFetches current, version-specific documentation and code examples for a library so the agent answers from real docs instead of stale training data."
   }
   ```
2. **Pin the version** — replace `<PIN_A_REAL_VERSION>` with a concrete published version from npm (`npm view @upstash/context7-mcp version`). Never ship `@latest` in the registry.
3. **Confirm the API key is truly optional** — Context7 runs on a free tier without a key; `optional: true` is what lets a user install it with zero setup. Confirm the env var name (`CONTEXT7_API_KEY`) from the README.
4. Run `npm run validate:mcp` — fix any schema/invariant error it prints. Keep the JSON valid (no trailing comma after your new object).

### How to verify done
- **Automated:** `npm run validate:mcp` passes; `npm test` still green.
- **Manual smoke:** `npm start`, open the toolkit store (툴킷/Toolkit → Store), confirm a **Context7** card appears under **All** and the **Dev** category with the right name/description, and that Install is offered (no OAuth prompt). Optionally install it and confirm the two tools show up.
- **Acceptance criteria:** exactly one new well-formed object in `entries[]`; `trustLevel: "needs_review"`; version pinned; validator + tests pass; the card renders in the store.

### Impact / risk
**LOW.** One data object in one JSON file, consumed by an already-built pipeline; no component/IPC/Flask code touched, no cross-layer coupling. The schema + custom invariant validator + CI catch mistakes before merge, and `needs_review` trust means it goes through the human security gate before being treated as trusted. No HIGH/CRITICAL paths.

title: i18n: toolkit store category filter tags not translated (missing store_category_* keys in 9 locales)
body: ### What & Why The MCP toolkit store has a row of category filter tags — **All / Browser / Dev / DevOps / Productivity / Workspace / Memory / Communication**. When the app UI is set to any language other than English or Simplified Chinese (e.g. Korean, as in the report screenshot), these tags render in **English** instead of the selected language. The rendering code is already correct — it looks up each label through `t()`. The real cause is that the 8 translation keys simply **do not exist** in the other 9 locale files, so the translation layer falls back to English. This is a good first issue: it's a self-contained i18n data fix with zero architectural risk, and it walks a newcomer through how PuPu's translation system works. ### Read this first - `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — project conventions (JS-only, inline styles, i18n via `t()`). - `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/mini_react/use_translation.js` — the translation hook. Note the fallback: lines 82–85 fall back to `en.json` when a key is missing in the active locale. **This fallback is exactly why the bug shows English text instead of a broken key.** - `src/locales/en.json` — the source-of-truth locale; every key that exists here should exist in all 10 other locale files. - Start the app with `npm start` (React on :2907 + Electron) to reproduce. ### Architecture at a glance Translation is a plain key-lookup: components call `t("toolkit.store_category_browser")`, and `use_translation.js` resolves that dotted key against the active locale's JSON (`src/locales/.json`), falling back to `en.json` if the key is absent. Category tags are defined once in `STORE_CATEGORY_CONFIG` as `{ key, icon, labelKey }` objects and rendered by the store page — no per-language logic lives in the component; the only thing missing is the data. ### Relevant files - `src/COMPONENTs/toolkit/constants.js:62` — `STORE_CATEGORY_CONFIG`, maps each category to a `labelKey` like `toolkit.store_category_browser`. **No change needed** — read it to see the 8 keys you must provide translations for. - `src/COMPONENTs/toolkit/pages/toolkit_store_page.js:38` — renders `t(item.labelKey)`. **No change needed** — confirms the code is already i18n-correct. - `src/locales/en.json` (`toolkit.store_category_*`) — the 8 English source strings to translate from. **No change needed**, reference only. - `src/locales/{zh-TW,de,es,fr,it,ja,ko,pt-BR,ru}.json` — **the 9 files to edit.** Each is missing all 8 keys under the `toolkit` object. The 8 keys and their English source values: | key | English | |---|---| | `toolkit.store_category_all` | All | | `toolkit.store_category_browser` | Browser | | `toolkit.store_category_dev` | Dev | | `toolkit.store_category_devops` | DevOps | | `toolkit.store_category_productivity` | Productivity | | `toolkit.store_category_workspace` | Workspace | | `toolkit.store_category_memory` | Memory | | `toolkit.store_category_communication` | Communication | ### Suggested development path 1. Open `src/locales/en.json`, find the `toolkit` object, and locate the 8 `store_category_*` keys — this is your reference block. 2. For each of the 9 target locale files, add the same 8 keys **inside the existing `toolkit` object** (the object already exists — don't create a new one), with the value translated into that language. Keep technical/brand-ish terms conventional per language (e.g. "Browser", "DevOps" are often left as-is or lightly localized — match how neighboring keys in that file handle such terms). 3. Self-check as you go: the JSON must stay valid (no trailing commas). After each file, `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('src/locales/ko.json'))"` should succeed. 4. Verify key parity with this one-liner (should report `0 missing` for every locale): ``` python3 -c "import json; en=json.load(open('src/locales/en.json'))['toolkit']; keys=[k for k in en if k.startswith('store_category')]; [print(l, sum(k not in json.load(open(f'src/locales/{l}.json')).get('toolkit',{}) for k in keys), 'missing') for l in ['zh-TW','de','es','fr','it','ja','ko','pt-BR','ru']]" ``` ### How to verify done - **Automated:** `npm test` passes (there is no dedicated i18n parity test today; the existing `use_translation.test.js` must still pass). The parity one-liner above reports `0 missing` for all 9 locales. - **Manual smoke:** `npm start`, switch the app language to Korean (설정 → language), open the toolkit store (툴킷 → 스토어). The category tags should now read in Korean, not English. Spot-check one more language. - **Acceptance criteria:** all 9 edited locale files contain the 8 `store_category_*` keys with sensible translations; all JSON stays valid; no English fallback remains for these tags in a non-en/non-zh-CN UI. ### Impact / risk **LOW.** The change is pure locale data consumed only by `t()` in `use_translation.js`; no component, IPC, or Flask code is touched, and there is no cross-layer coupling. Worst-case failure is a malformed JSON file, caught immediately by `npm start` failing to compile or the `json.load` self-check. No HIGH/CRITICAL paths involved. > **Optional note for the assignee (not required for this ticket):** these 8 keys are part of a larger gap — the same 9 locales are each missing ~143 `toolkit.* / local_storage.* / dev.*` keys total. This ticket is intentionally scoped to just the store category tags; the broader gap can be follow-up issues.

title: Add production 120 Hz UI performance observability and regression budgets
body:
### What & Why

PuPu currently calls `reportWebVitals()` without a consumer and has no production Long Animation Frame/long-task collection, route-level User Timing, React render budgets, or repeatable CI performance scenarios. As a result, performance regressions are found by feel after they land. This issue establishes a lightweight, privacy-safe performance service and a deterministic Electron performance gate for the interactions that define PuPu's perceived quality.

### Read this first

You are assumed to have zero context on this project. Read in this order:

1. `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — JavaScript-only frontend, inline-style rules, preload IPC boundaries, and test conventions.
2. `docs/DEV_GUIDE.md` — documentation index and verification entry points.
3. `docs/architecture/request-flow-and-streaming.md` — renderer, Electron, sidecar, and streaming ownership boundaries.
4. `src/index.js` and `src/reportWebVitals.js` — current unused web-vitals entry point.

Environment: `npm start` runs React on port 2907 plus Electron. Use production behavior for performance sign-off; jsdom tests are necessary but not sufficient.

### Architecture at a glance

```text
User Timing + web vitals + Long Animation Frame observer
  → privacy-safe local performance service
    → development overlay / exported diagnostic snapshot
    → scripted production Electron golden scenarios
      → CI budgets and release sign-off
```

Key facts established by investigation:

- `src/index.js` calls `reportWebVitals()` with no callback, so current vitals are discarded.
- The July audit measured healthy 120Hz idle behavior but confirmed long-chat DOM explosion, runtime-event scaling, sidebar layout bursts, cold-input spikes, and large Chinese-font startup cost.
- A promise of 'no visible jank' requires hard scenario budgets; component unit tests alone cannot detect layout, paint, GPU, or main-thread stalls.

### Relevant files

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `src/index.js` | Wire the performance service at app startup. |
| `src/reportWebVitals.js` | Forward supported metrics without external telemetry by default. |
| `src/SERVICEs/ui_performance.js` | New privacy-safe collector for marks, measures, long tasks/frames, and bounded diagnostics. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/ui-testing/` | Add deterministic data/scenarios for long chat, trace, sidebar, input, and editors. |
| `scripts/` | Launch a production Electron build with isolated userData and collect CDP metrics/traces. |
| `package.json` | Expose focused performance commands and release gate. |

### Suggested development path

1. Define golden scenarios and budgets before adding instrumentation: 10k-message navigation, 10k runtime events, cold input, sidebar toggle, 100-node FlowEditor, 10k-point Memory Scatter, large Markdown/diff, and a cold `zh-CN` launch with an empty font cache.
2. Collect INP/web vitals plus Long Animation Frame or long-task entries, bounded to recent samples and stripped of message content/file paths.
3. Add User Timing marks around chat switch, stream flush, runtime-event reduction, Markdown commit, modal first open, and storage bootstrap.
4. Build an isolated production Electron runner that records DOM nodes, listeners, heap, task/script/layout/style durations, and frame intervals.
5. Start with deterministic release gates of: bounded chat DOM <= 40 mounted messages; runtime-event batch p95 <= 8.33ms; interaction main-thread work p95 <= 8.33ms; dropped-frame ratio <= 1%; and zero tasks over 50ms. Tightening or relaxing a gate requires recorded production evidence. Keep noisy GPU comparisons and cold-font timing advisory until the reference hardware/profile is calibrated.

### How to verify done

- [ ] Developers can export one bounded diagnostic snapshot without exposing chat content.
- [ ] Golden scenarios run against a production build and isolated profile.
- [ ] 120Hz animation scenarios report frame P95, dropped-frame ratio, and long tasks against the documented <= 8.33ms / <= 1% / zero-over-50ms gates.
- [ ] 10k-message DOM stays at or below 40 mounted messages; 10k-event batch p95 stays at or below 8.33ms.
- [ ] A cold `zh-CN` launch with an empty font cache records first paint, interactive readiness, font-load duration, and long tasks without capturing user content.
- [ ] The strict `CI=1` production build is green and performance budgets are documented.

### Impact / risk

> Blast radius was assessed from the July 2026 UI performance audit. GitNexus was stale and its rebuild was blocked by the local LadybugDB FTS extension, so treat the manual hot-path analysis below as authoritative until the index is healthy.

**HIGH:**
- Instrumentation must never capture prompt text, tool arguments, file contents, API keys, or stable personal identifiers.

**MEDIUM:**
- Headless/virtualized GPU timings are noisy. Separate deterministic main-thread budgets from advisory paint/GPU budgets.

title: Unmount hidden SideMenu workload after the exit transition
body:
### What & Why

Closing SideMenu currently changes its width to zero but leaves Explorer, chat-store subscriptions, DnD listeners, the relative-time interval, character availability requests, search, images, and modal launchers mounted. The invisible sidebar therefore continues consuming CPU, memory, network/IPC, and observer work during normal chat use. This issue separates the lightweight shell/toggle from the heavy content and unmounts the latter after the exit transition while preserving its state.

### Read this first

You are assumed to have zero context on this project. Read in this order:

1. `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — JavaScript-only frontend, inline-style rules, preload IPC boundaries, and test conventions.
2. `docs/DEV_GUIDE.md` — documentation index and verification entry points.
3. `docs/architecture/request-flow-and-streaming.md` — renderer, Electron, sidecar, and streaming ownership boundaries.
4. `src/COMPONENTs/side-menu/hooks/use_chat_tree_store.js` and `use_character_availability.js` — current subscription/polling lifetimes.

Environment: `npm start` runs React on port 2907 plus Electron. Use production behavior for performance sign-off; jsdom tests are necessary but not sufficient.

### Architecture at a glance

```text
ConfigContainer always mounts SideMenu
  → closed today: width=0, heavy subtree remains alive
  → target: shell remains; content exits → unmount
             state/cache lives outside the transient subtree
```

Key facts established by investigation:

- SideMenu is always mounted by `ConfigContainer`.
- `useChatTreeStore` subscribes to broad chat-store changes even while closed.
- `useCharacterAvailability` can refetch all character ids and keep a minute interval alive.
- Explorer owns DnD, row/cache, measurement, and global interaction machinery that has no value while invisible.

### Relevant files

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `src/CONTAINERs/config/container.js` | Keep the shell mounted without forcing heavy content lifetime. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/side-menu/side_menu.js` | Split shell from content and coordinate exit completion. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/side-menu/hooks/use_chat_tree_store.js` | Subscribe only while content is active or use selectors. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/side-menu/hooks/use_character_availability.js` | Pause polling and stabilize the character-id key. |
| `src/BUILTIN_COMPONENTs/explorer/explorer.js` | Preserve externalized expansion/selection state across remount. |

### Suggested development path

1. Inventory all listeners, observers, timers, subscriptions, and requests owned by the closed sidebar.
2. Split `SideMenuShell` from `SideMenuContent`; keep only the reveal/toggle surface in the shell.
3. Unmount content after the existing exit duration using the shared exit/unmount primitive.
4. Externalize search, expansion, selection, and row-cache state only where users expect it to survive reopen.
5. Abort availability requests and remove intervals/listeners on exit; refresh once on reopen.

### How to verify done

- [ ] After close, Explorer DOM, DnD listeners, character polling, and the relative-time interval are absent.
- [ ] Reopening preserves chat selection, expanded tree nodes, the current search query, and scroll position; transient hover, drag/drop, inline-edit, and popover state resets.
- [ ] Opening Settings/Tools/Agents from the sidebar still works after repeated remounts.
- [ ] 100 open/close cycles do not grow listener count or heap.
- [ ] `window.pupuChatTreeAPI` remains callable while content is unmounted and after repeated reopen cycles.
- [ ] SideMenu and Explorer tests pass.

### Impact / risk

body:
### What & Why

The renderer still exposes synchronous chat-storage reads through preload and invokes them during bootstrap/cold access. `sendSync` blocks Chromium's main renderer thread until Electron main and SQLite/storage work return, so any cold disk, migration, or main-process contention becomes visible UI jank.
