title: Security: default-require confirmation for MCP tools (F-FLASK-01) — no more self-declared gating
body:
### What & Why

PuPu pauses the stream and asks the user before executing dangerous tools — but for third-party MCP tools, **whether a tool needs confirmation is declared by the tool itself**. The engine defaults every MCP tool to `requires_confirmation=False` and only flips it when the server self-reports `annotations.destructiveHint=True`. In other words, the entity being gated decides whether the gate applies. A prompt-injected model (via a poisoned workspace file, tool output, or pasted content) can invoke any installed MCP tool that "forgot" to declare itself destructive — fetch, filesystem, shell wrappers — and **no confirmation dialog ever appears**. This is finding **F-FLASK-01 (High, verified)** from PuPu's first security investigation (SEC-001, 2026-06-10); it was consciously accepted at low exposure, but it is now a hard prerequisite for 0.2.0's auto-setup agent (which will *install MCP servers automatically*) and should land before the 0.1.9 exposure push. The fix: **flip the server-side default to require confirmation for all non-builtin tools**, downgrade only on explicit safe signals, and prove it with a red-team test.

### Read this first

You are assumed to have zero context on this project. Read in this order:

1. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — project conventions and architecture map.
2. `docs/features/toolkit-and-tool-catalog.md` — how toolkits are discovered, attached to the agent, and how the confirmation flow pauses the SSE stream.
3. `docs/architecture/request-flow-and-streaming.md` — the streaming pipeline the confirmation frames travel through.
4. `.claude/security/sec-001/findings-flask.md` — the original F-FLASK-01 finding (report anchors are from 2026-06; current line numbers are below).
5. MCP spec on [tool annotations](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools#toolannotations) — `destructiveHint`, `readOnlyHint`, and why annotations are explicitly *untrusted hints*.

Environment: `npm start` for the full stack; the Python sidecar standalone via `cd unchain_runtime/server && python main.py`. **This task spans two repos** — the engine fix lands in the separate `unchain` Python library; PuPu consumes it and carries the catalog/UI surface.

### Architecture at a glance

The confirmation gate, end to end:

```
MCP server declares tools (+ optional annotations)
  → unchain MCPToolkit._convert_mcp_tool            ← THE FLAW: default False,
      sets requires_confirmation from destructiveHint  only server-declared destructive flips it
    → AgentBuilder flattens tools onto the agent
      → tool executes → confirmation.py:106-110 checks tool_obj.requires_confirmation
          (a ToolConfirmationPolicy can only NARROW this, never RAISE it)
        → if True: emit tool_call frame w/ confirmation_id → SSE pause → UI dialog
        → if False: silent execution
```

Key facts established by investigation (line numbers current, not the 2026-06 report's):

- The runtime gate: `unchain/tools/confirmation.py:106` — `requires_confirmation = bool(tool_obj and tool_obj.requires_confirmation)`; a `ToolConfirmationPolicy` at line 108 is ANDed in, so a policy can only *narrow* confirmation. **The default must therefore be set at tool-construction time — you cannot fix this purely with a policy hook.**
- The flaw: `unchain/toolkits/mcp.py:320-326` — `requires_confirmation = False`, flipped to `True` only if `annotations.destructiveHint is True`. `readOnlyHint` is not consulted; absence of annotations = no confirmation.
- Builtin `core` tools are gated correctly and independently (`unchain/toolkits/builtin/core/coding_backend.py:687+` returns `ToolConfirmationPolicy(requires_confirmation=True)` for write/edit/shell), so the fix must **not** disturb builtin behavior.
- PuPu today has **no server-side override for MCP**: `unchain_adapter.py` only force-confirms builtin workspace/terminal tools; the catalog just mirrors the tool's self-declared flag (`mcp_toolkits.py:503-511` `_tool_to_dict`, `unchain_adapter.py:1980-2000` for `toolkit.toml` entries).
- There is a user-facing auto-approve store (`src/SERVICEs/toolkit_auto_approve_store.js`) — the fix must interoperate with it: default-deny at the server, user can still opt a specific tool into auto-approval.

### Relevant files

**unchain repo (engine — the core fix):**

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `src/unchain/toolkits/mcp.py:320-339` | `_convert_mcp_tool`: flip the default to `requires_confirmation=True`; downgrade only on `readOnlyHint is True` (and/or an explicit trusted-allowlist signal). **The primary change.** |
| `src/unchain/tools/confirmation.py:106-110` | Read-only reference: confirms a policy can only narrow, so the default belongs upstream. |
| `src/unchain/toolkits/builtin/core/coding_backend.py:687+` | Read-only reference: builtin gating is separate and must stay unchanged. |
| `tests/` (mirror `test_*mcp*`/toolkit tests) | New unit test: a converted MCP tool with no annotations must come out `requires_confirmation=True`; `readOnlyHint=True` comes out `False`. |

**PuPu repo (surface + red-team test):**

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `unchain_runtime/server/mcp_toolkits.py:499-512` | `_tool_to_dict`: catalog now reflects the safe default; verify it reads through. |
| `unchain_runtime/server/unchain_adapter.py:1980-2000` | `toolkit.toml` confirmation normalization — ensure a trusted-toolkit allowlist (builtin `core`/`plan`/`agent_reach`) is the *only* way to skip the default. |
| `src/SERVICEs/toolkit_auto_approve_store.js` | Confirm user auto-approve still overrides the new default (opt-in per tool), so the safe default is not a UX regression. |
| `unchain_runtime/server/` (route/test for chat confirmation) | Home for the red-team integration test below. |
| `.claude/security/sec-001/findings-flask.md` + `DECISION.md` | Update F-FLASK-01 status from "accepted" to "fixed" once merged. |

### Suggested development path

1. **Reproduce the hole.** Install (or stub) an MCP server exposing a tool with **no** `destructiveHint`. In a chat, get the model to call it. Confirm today: it executes with **no** confirmation dialog. This is your failing baseline.
2. **Flip the engine default (`unchain/toolkits/mcp.py`).** Change the default to `requires_confirmation=True`. Downgrade to `False` only when `annotations.readOnlyHint is True` (a positive safe signal), never on mere absence. Self-check: unit test both cases (no annotations → True; `readOnlyHint=True` → False).
3. **Add the trusted allowlist.** Ensure only builtin toolkits (`core`, `plan`, `agent_reach`) bypass the default — MCP and workspace `toolkit.toml` tools are subject to it unless the toml *explicitly* sets `requires_confirmation=false` (an author's deliberate opt-out, not a silent default). Wire this in `unchain_adapter.py:1980-2000`.
4. **Verify builtins are untouched.** Run the existing core-toolkit confirmation tests — write/edit/shell must still confirm, read/glob/grep must still not. Zero diff in builtin behavior.
5. **Interop with auto-approve.** Confirm a user who auto-approves a specific MCP tool still skips the dialog for it — default-deny at the server, explicit user opt-in still wins. This keeps power users unblocked.
6. **Write the red-team test.** Integration test: register a stub MCP server whose tool declares no `destructiveHint`; drive a chat message that induces the model to call it; **assert a `tool_call` frame with a `confirmation_id` is emitted** and execution blocks until approval. This test is the regression guard for F-FLASK-01.
7. **Update the security record.** Flip F-FLASK-01 to "fixed" in `sec-001/`.

### How to verify done

- [ ] A converted MCP tool with no annotations has `requires_confirmation=True` (engine unit test).
- [ ] An MCP tool with `readOnlyHint=True` has `requires_confirmation=False` (engine unit test).
- [ ] Red-team integration test passes: a non-`destructiveHint` MCP tool call **emits a confirmation frame and blocks** until the user approves.
- [ ] Builtin `core` tools unchanged: `write`/`edit`/`shell` still confirm; `read`/`glob`/`grep` still don't (existing tests green).
- [ ] A user-set auto-approval for a specific MCP tool still bypasses the dialog (no power-user regression).
- [ ] The toolkit catalog served to the frontend reports the corrected `requiresConfirmation` values.
- [ ] Manual smoke via the pupu-test-api skill: install a stub MCP tool, send a tool-inducing message, observe the confirmation dialog appear.
- [ ] `npm test` passes; unchain `./run_tests.sh` passes.
- [ ] F-FLASK-01 marked fixed in `.claude/security/sec-001/`.

### Impact / risk

> Blast radius assessed by manual cross-repo investigation (GitNexus impact analysis unavailable in the authoring session).

**HIGH — this is a security fix that changes default behavior for every MCP tool:**
- `mcp.py:_convert_mcp_tool` runs for **every** MCP tool on **every** agent build. Correct default-deny is the whole point; a mistake that leaves it default-allow silently reopens the hole. The red-team test is mandatory, not optional.
- Must not touch the builtin `core` confirmation path — a regression there would either spam users with confirmations on safe reads or (worse) stop confirming writes/shell.

**MEDIUM — UX regression risk if overcorrected:**
- Flipping to default-confirm means read-only MCP tools without a `readOnlyHint` will now prompt. That is the *safe* direction, but note it in release notes; rely on `readOnlyHint` + the auto-approve store to keep friction down. Do not add broad silent exceptions to dampen prompts — that would recreate F-FLASK-01.
- Confirmation catalog shape (`requiresConfirmation`) is consumed by the frontend; keep the field contract stable.

title: Add Gemini provider end-to-end: native driver with streaming, tool calling, and prompt caching (0.1.9)
body:
### What & Why

PuPu supports OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama as chat providers; Gemini is a locked 0.1.9 roadmap item and is currently absent end-to-end. Curiously, most of the scaffolding already exists — the shared capability catalog ships `gemini-2.5-pro` / `gemini-2.5-flash` entries, a Gemini message builder and structured-output formatter live in the engine, and a Gemini logo icon is already registered in PuPu — but **the actual driver class is missing**, and PuPu's frontend/backend actively filter the provider out at ~12 hard-coded sites. This issue adds a **native Gemini driver** to the `unchain` engine (streaming, tool calling, **prompt caching** with cache-token accounting) plus a **JSON-schema sanitizer** for Gemini's stricter function-declaration schema, opens PuPu's provider plumbing (API key storage, settings UI, model selector, catalog), cleans up stale/inconsistent Gemini references, and lands a **minimal eval gate** so model-visible behavior is verified before release. User value: Gemini's price/performance (especially Flash) is a major draw for exactly the audience PuPu targets.

### Read this first

You are assumed to have zero context on this project. Read in this order:

1. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — project conventions (JavaScript only, inline styles, IPC boundary rules).
2. `docs/DEV_GUIDE.md` — documentation index.
3. `docs/architecture/request-flow-and-streaming.md` — how a chat message travels React → Electron IPC → Flask → the unchain engine → provider SDK.
4. `docs/data-models/model-and-toolkit-catalog.md` — the model catalog / capability data shape.
5. Gemini API docs: [text generation & streaming](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/text-generation), [function calling](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling), [context caching](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/caching) — implicit vs explicit caching matters below.

Environment: `npm start` runs the full dev stack (React on port 2907 + Electron). The Python sidecar runs standalone via `cd unchain_runtime/server && python main.py`. You need a Gemini API key (free tier is fine: https://aistudio.google.com). The `google.genai` SDK is already installed in the engine's venv.

**This task spans two repos.** The AI engine (`unchain`) is a separate Python library that PuPu's Flask sidecar imports. The driver lands in `unchain`; the plumbing/UI lands in PuPu.

### Architecture at a glance

```
Settings UI (stores gemini_api_key in localStorage settings.model_providers)
  → chat payload: injectProviderApiKeyIntoPayload() adds geminiApiKey
    → Flask: unchain_adapter.py extracts key, builds UnchainAgent(provider="gemini", ...)
      → unchain: ModelIOFactoryRegistry creates GeminiModelIO   ← DOES NOT EXIST YET
        → fetch_turn() streams from Gemini API, parses tool calls,
          reports token usage incl. cached tokens
      ← SSE frames flow back: Flask → Electron IPC → React handlers
```

Key facts established by investigation:

**Engine (unchain) — what exists vs missing:**
- Driver contract: `providers/base.py` `ModelIO` protocol (`provider` attr + `fetch_turn(ModelTurnRequest) -> ModelTurnResult`); subclass `_NativeModelIOBase` (`providers/native.py:285`) for payload/capability helpers.
- **Missing: `GeminiModelIO`.** Not present in `providers/`, not registered in either registry (`providers/registry.py:6-17` and `agent/model_io.py:12-17` — both must get entries).
- **Already exists:** `GeminiMessageBuilder` (`tools/messages.py:63`, native `parts`/`function_response` shape), `ResponseFormat.to_gemini` (`schemas/response.py:46`), capability + default-payload JSON entries for `gemini-2.5-pro`/`-flash`, eval env mapping (`tests/evals/env.py:15` → `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY`).
- **Prompt-caching reference:** `anthropic.py` injects `cache_control` blocks (lines 83-98) and accounts `cache_read_input_tokens`/`cache_creation_input_tokens` (224-235, 260-267); `openai.py` only reports `cached_tokens` (262-273). `ModelTurnResult`/`TokenUsage` already carry both cache fields (`kernel/types.py:31-32, 47-48`). Gemini maps `cachedContentTokenCount` → `cache_read_input_tokens`.
- **Schema gap:** `Tool.to_provider_json` (`tools/tool.py:261`) has no `gemini` branch — Gemini would silently get the OpenAI shape. Worse, `_parameters_json_schema` (line 234) always emits `additionalProperties: false`, which Gemini's function-declaration schema **rejects**. A sanitizer (strip `additionalProperties`, flatten unsupported `anyOf`/`$ref`/`format` keywords) is net-new work.
- **Stale entry:** `schemas/models.py:203` defines `GEMINI_PRO_15` with `provider="google"` — both the model (1.5) and the provider name (`google` vs `gemini`) are inconsistent with everything else. Tests `tests/test_new_models.py:36-45` pin the wrong value.

**PuPu — the provider set `{ollama, openai, anthropic}` is hard-coded at ~12 sites (all must add `gemini`):**
- Backend `unchain_adapter.py`: `_SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` (99), default-model maps (244-247, 680-685), override allow-lists (717/724/734, 747/750/756), **catalog filter that currently drops Gemini entries** (`get_capability_catalog`, 1065-1074), max-tokens param branch (2363-2371), API-key extraction (2658-2680 — binary openai/anthropic else), env fallback + required-key set (3086-3102), and the chat-title summary generator which directly instantiates SDKs (2981-3025).
- Backend `route_catalog.py:54-58`: hand-built `providers` response object.
- Frontend: `api.shared.js` `EMPTY_MODEL_CATALOG` (17-29) + `normalizeModelCatalog` (296-300); `api.unchain.js` `SUPPORTED_REMOTE_PROVIDERS` (17), `getStoredProviderApiKey` (108-127), camel-key mapping (145-146); settings UI (`settings/model_providers/index.js` — add a `GeminiSection`); init-setup wizard (`init-setup/steps/configure_providers.js:379-387, 514-534`); model selector (`chat-input/constants.js:8-18`, `build_model_options.js:12-74`, `use_chat_input_models.js:24-43`); chat hero chips + provider icon map (`chat.js:49-56, 182, 556, 798-816`). Icon key `"gemini"` already exists (`icon_manifest.js:1382`).
- Stale UI entry: `agents/pages/recipes_page/detail_panel/agent_panel.js:16` hard-codes bare `gemini-2.5-pro` (missing the `gemini:` prefix convention).
- **Eval infrastructure: confirmed none exists** (all `eval` hits are the unrelated character-availability feature). The eval gate below is intentionally minimal.

### Relevant files

**unchain repo (engine):**

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `src/unchain/providers/gemini.py` | **New.** `GeminiModelIO(_NativeModelIOBase)`, `provider="gemini"`, `fetch_turn` over `google.genai` streaming. |
| `src/unchain/providers/native.py` | Add `_translate_content_blocks_for_gemini` (contents/parts/inline_data), alongside the existing anthropic (117) / openai (198) translators. |
| `src/unchain/providers/registry.py` + `agent/model_io.py` + `providers/__init__.py` | Register the driver in **both** registries (+ `_create_gemini` reading `GEMINI_API_KEY`/`GOOGLE_API_KEY`) and export it. |
| `src/unchain/tools/tool.py` | Add the `gemini` branch to `to_provider_json` + the JSON-schema sanitizer. |
| `src/unchain/providers/anthropic.py`, `openai.py` | Read-only references: streaming loop, tool-call assembly, cache-token accounting. |
| `src/unchain/schemas/models.py:203` + `tests/test_new_models.py:36-45` | Reconcile stale `GEMINI_PRO_15` / `provider="google"`. |
| `tests/test_hyperspace_model_io.py` | The best template for a full provider-driver test. |

**PuPu repo:**

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `unchain_runtime/server/unchain_adapter.py` | All the allow-list/default/key/summary sites enumerated above. |
| `unchain_runtime/server/route_catalog.py` | Add `gemini` to the providers response (54-58). |
| `src/SERVICEs/api.shared.js`, `api.unchain.js` | Catalog shape + key injection. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/settings/model_providers/index.js` (+ `storage.js`) | New `GeminiSection` with `storage_key="gemini_api_key"`. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/init-setup/steps/configure_providers.js` | First-run wizard: `PROVIDER_META` + substep branch. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/chat-input/` (constants, build_model_options, use_chat_input_models) | Model selector grouping + `gemini:` prefix. |
| `src/PAGEs/chat/chat.js` | Provider icon map + hero model chips. |
| `src/COMPONENTs/agents/pages/recipes_page/detail_panel/agent_panel.js:16` | Fix bare `gemini-2.5-pro` → prefixed convention. |
| `docs/data-models/model-and-toolkit-catalog.md` | Document the new provider. |

### Suggested development path

Work engine-out. Each numbered step is independently testable.

1. **Spike: confirm native driver over OpenAI-compat shortcut (½ day, timeboxed).** Gemini exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint that would let PuPu reuse `OpenAIModelIO`. Verify what the roadmap already suspected: the compat layer cannot express explicit context caching, thinking budgets, or Gemini-native tool schemas, and the engine's existing Gemini scaffolding (`GeminiMessageBuilder`, `to_gemini`) is native-shaped. Unless the spike overturns this, proceed native; record the decision in the PR description.
2. **Build `GeminiModelIO` (unchain).** Implement `fetch_turn`: build `contents` from messages via the new translator, attach `tools` (functionDeclarations) from the sanitized schema, stream chunks (emit via `self._emit`), assemble `ToolCall`s from `functionCall` parts, populate `TokenUsage` — mapping `usageMetadata.cachedContentTokenCount` → `cache_read_input_tokens`. Self-check: unit tests mirroring `test_hyperspace_model_io.py` with a faked SDK.
3. **Schema sanitizer.** In the `gemini` branch of `to_provider_json`: strip `additionalProperties`, handle `anyOf`/`$ref`/unsupported `format` values. Unit-test against every built-in tool's real schema — all must pass Gemini's validator shape.
4. **Prompt caching.** Implicit caching is automatic on 2.5 models — verify cached-token counts flow through `TokenUsage` into PuPu's token-usage display. Add explicit caching only if the implicit path proves insufficient for PuPu's long-system-prompt pattern (measure first; the Anthropic driver's cache_control pattern is the reference if needed).
5. **Register + reconcile.** Both registries, `__init__.py` export, fix `provider="google"` → `"gemini"` in `schemas/models.py` (+ its test), remove/replace the stale 1.5 model entry.
6. **Open PuPu's backend.** Add `gemini` at every `unchain_adapter.py` site listed above + `route_catalog.py`. The catalog entries will surface automatically once the filter at 1065-1074 is opened. Add the summary-generator branch (`google.genai`) so chat titles work.
7. **Open PuPu's frontend.** Key storage/injection, `GeminiSection` in settings, init-setup wizard, model selector, hero chips, icon map. Follow the Anthropic sibling in each file — every site has an exact pattern to copy. Inline styles + `isDark` per conventions.
8. **Minimal eval gate.** No eval infra exists; build the smallest useful gate, not a framework: a pytest-marked live smoke suite (skipped without `GEMINI_API_KEY`) asserting (a) streamed text completion, (b) a tool round-trip on a built-in tool, (c) structured output via `to_gemini`, (d) `cache_read_input_tokens > 0` on a repeated long-context call, (e) the same suite passes for openai/anthropic (regression guard). This suite is the release gate for this feature and the seed of the 0.1.10 eval workstream.
9. **Cleanup + docs.** Fix `agent_panel.js:16`, update `docs/data-models/model-and-toolkit-catalog.md` and the two docs pages that already advertise Gemini.

### How to verify done

- [ ] Settings → Model Providers shows a Gemini section; entering a key persists as `settings.model_providers.gemini_api_key`.
- [ ] Init-setup wizard offers Gemini as a provider option.
- [ ] Model selector lists `gemini-2.5-pro` / `gemini-2.5-flash` under a "Gemini" group (with icon) once a key is stored; hero chips render.
- [ ] Streaming chat works end-to-end on `gemini:gemini-2.5-flash` — tokens render live, chat title generates.
- [ ] Tool calling works: `core` toolkit file-read round-trip completes; confirmation-required tools still pause the stream.
- [ ] Every built-in tool's schema passes Gemini's function-declaration validation (no `additionalProperties` rejections).
- [ ] Token usage display shows non-zero cached tokens on a repeated long-context conversation.
- [ ] OpenAI, Anthropic, and Ollama behavior is byte-identical (regression smoke of the eval suite).
- [ ] `npm test` passes; unchain `./run_tests.sh` passes; the new live eval suite passes with a real key.
- [ ] Stale `provider="google"` / bare `gemini-2.5-pro` references are gone (`rg -i "gemini"` audit is clean).

### Impact / risk

> Blast radius assessed by manual cross-repo investigation (GitNexus impact analysis unavailable in the authoring session).

**HIGH:**
- `unchain_adapter.py` is touched at ~10 sites including the API-key path shared by **all** remote providers — a mistake in `_extract_api_key_from_options` / `_resolve_agent_api_key` breaks OpenAI/Anthropic chat, not just Gemini. Keep existing branches byte-identical; add, don't restructure.
- `api.unchain.js` key injection runs on **every** stream start for every provider.

**MEDIUM:**
- The schema sanitizer changes tool schemas sent to Gemini only — but a bug that leaks into the shared `_parameters_json_schema` would alter tool behavior on all providers. Keep sanitization inside the `gemini` branch.
- `normalizeModelCatalog` / `EMPTY_MODEL_CATALOG` shape changes touch a documented data contract — update the docs in the same PR.
- Live eval suite depends on an external API (flakiness); mark it clearly and keep it out of the default CI path, but required for this feature's sign-off.

title: Ollama: enable tool calling for models without native tool support (prompt-based emulation)
body:
### What & Why

PuPu currently supports tool calling only for models that natively implement it. For Ollama, tool support is decided by a static, hand-maintained flag (`supports_tools`) — when a model is flagged `false` (today only `deepseek-r1:14b`), PuPu silently hides the toolkit selector and strips all tools from the request; when a locally-pulled model is *not* in the catalog, PuPu wrongly assumes it supports tools and sends them anyway, with no error handling if the model rejects them. The goal of this issue is to make **every Ollama chat model usable with tools**, by adding a **prompt-based tool-calling emulation layer**: when a model has no native tool support, tool schemas are injected into the prompt, and tool calls are parsed out of the model's text output — transparently to the rest of the system. User value: people running local models (a core PuPu audience) get the full agent experience regardless of which model they pulled.

### Read this first

You are assumed to have zero context on this project. Read in this order:

1. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` — project conventions (JavaScript only, inline styles, IPC boundary rules).
2. `docs/DEV_GUIDE.md` — full documentation index.
3. `docs/architecture/request-flow-and-streaming.md` — how a chat message travels React → Electron IPC → Flask → the unchain engine → provider.
4. `docs/features/toolkit-and-tool-catalog.md` — how toolkits are discovered, selected per chat, and attached to the agent.
5. `docs/data-models/model-and-toolkit-catalog.md` — the model-capability data shape.

Environment: `npm start` runs the full dev stack (React on port 2907 + Electron). The Python sidecar can run standalone: `cd unchain_runtime/server && python main.py`. You need a local [Ollama](https://ollama.com) install with at least one non-tool model pulled (`ollama pull deepseek-r1:14b`) and one tool-capable model (e.g. `ollama pull qwen3`) for comparison.

**Note: this task spans two repos.** The AI engine (`unchain`) is a separate library that PuPu's Flask sidecar imports. The emulation core lands in `unchain`; the capability plumbing and UI changes land in PuPu.

### Architecture at a glance

The slice you care about — how tools reach an Ollama model:

```
Chat page (src/PAGEs/chat/chat.js)
  gates toolkit selection on supports_tools        ← UI gate (currently hides tools)
  → useChatStream sends payload {selectedToolkits}
    → Flask: unchain_runtime/server/unchain_adapter.py
      builds UnchainAgent, attaches tools
      → unchain kernel loop (src/unchain/kernel/loop.py)
        → OllamaModelIO.fetch_turn (src/unchain/providers/ollama.py)
          POSTs {OLLAMA_HOST}/api/chat with body["tools"]   ← native-only today
          parses streamed message.tool_calls → ToolCall[]
        ← kernel loop executes tools, appends results, re-calls fetch_turn
```

Capability data flow: `unchain/src/unchain/runtime/resources/model_capabilities.json` (static JSON) → `unchain_adapter.py` catalog builders → `/models/catalog` endpoint → `api.shared.js` normalization → `chat.js` gating boolean `modelSupportsTools`.

Key facts established by investigation:

- The Ollama driver attaches tools **only if** `supports_tools` is truthy (`ollama.py:48`); otherwise tools are silently omitted.
- There is **no prompt-based fallback anywhere** — `unchain/src/unchain/tools/prompting.py` (`render_tool_prompt_block`) renders human-readable tool *guidance* but never parses tool calls from text.
- There is **no error handling** for Ollama's `400 "…does not support tools"` — it surfaces as a raw `ValueError` (`ollama.py:81-88`).
- Models absent from the JSON **default to tool-capable** — newly pulled non-tool models fail unguarded.
- The UI gate (`chat.js:275`, `modelSupportsTools`) hides the toolkit selector entirely and empties `effectiveSelectedToolkits` — a silent drop with no user-facing notice.

### Relevant files

**unchain repo (engine — emulation core):**

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `src/unchain/providers/ollama.py` | The only Ollama driver. `fetch_turn` (lines 39-166) builds the request, gates tools on `supports_tools` (line 48), parses native `message.tool_calls` (lines 124-151). **The emulation lives here.** |
| `src/unchain/tools/prompting.py` | `render_tool_prompt_block` / `ToolPromptHarness` — existing tool-schema-to-prompt renderer to reuse/extend for injection. |
| `src/unchain/tools/tool.py` | `Tool.to_provider_json` (lines 261-287) — canonical tool schema shapes. |
| `src/unchain/providers/native.py` | `_model_capability` (lines 331-336) + capabilities loading (lines 288-309) — how the driver knows `supports_tools`. |
| `src/unchain/runtime/resources/model_capabilities.json` | Static capability catalog; `deepseek-r1:14b` is the one `supports_tools: false` entry. |
| `src/unchain/kernel/loop.py` | Tool dispatch phases (lines 239-259). You should NOT need to change it — emulation must stay transparent to the loop. |

**PuPu repo (plumbing + UI):**

| File | Why you'll touch it |
|---|---|
| `unchain_runtime/server/unchain_adapter.py` | Catalog builders: `_normalize_model_capabilities` (983-995), `get_model_capability_catalog` (1135-1154), `_fetch_ollama_models` (1038-1061, plain `/api/tags`). Expose the new "emulated" mode in the catalog. |
| `src/SERVICEs/api.shared.js` | `normalizeModelInputCapabilities` (204-221) — mirror the new capability field. |
| `src/PAGEs/chat/chat.js` | `modelSupportsTools` gate (line 275), forced-empty toolkits (283-306), hidden selectors (701-702). **Un-hide tools for emulated models**, ideally with an "emulated" hint. |
| `docs/data-models/model-and-toolkit-catalog.md` | Update the capability shape documentation. |

### Suggested development path

Work engine-out: make emulation correct in isolation before touching UI.

1. **Reproduce the baseline.** Pull `deepseek-r1:14b`, select it in PuPu, observe: toolkit selector vanishes, no tools sent. Then hand-edit `model_capabilities.json` to remove the `supports_tools: false` flag and observe the unguarded failure mode. Now you understand both current behaviors.
2. **Build the emulation in `OllamaModelIO.fetch_turn` (unchain).** When `supports_tools` is false: (a) skip `body["tools"]`; (b) render tool schemas into a system-prompt block instructing the model to emit tool calls as a strict fenced JSON block (reuse/extend `render_tool_prompt_block`); (c) parse that block from the streamed `content` into `ToolCall` objects and return `ModelTurnResult(tool_calls=...)` — exactly mirroring the native parse at lines 124-151, so the kernel loop cannot tell the difference. Self-check: unit-test the parser against malformed output (truncated JSON, prose around the block, multiple blocks, no block at all → graceful plain-text turn).
3. **Handle tool results on the return trip.** Non-tool model templates may not render `tool`-role messages; when emulating, fold tool results into a plainly-formatted user-role message instead. Self-check: a two-step tool chain (call → result → model uses result) completes.
4. **Add error-driven fallback.** Catch Ollama's `400 "…does not support tools"` (`ollama.py:81-88` and the streamed-error path at 97-98) and retry the turn in emulated mode, so unlisted non-tool models degrade gracefully instead of erroring. Self-check: remove the JSON flag again, chat with tools — it should transparently fall back.
5. **Plumb capability mode through PuPu.** Extend the catalog so the frontend can distinguish `native` / `emulated` tool support (keep the boolean for compat; add a mode field). Update `_normalize_model_capabilities`, `api.shared.js`, and the docs.
6. **Un-gate the UI.** In `chat.js`, stop hiding the toolkit selector and stop emptying `effectiveSelectedToolkits` for emulated models; show a small "tools emulated — reliability depends on the model" notice (follow the existing `attachmentsDisabledReason` pattern at 277-281). Inline styles + `isDark`, per project conventions.
7. **Streaming trace sanity.** Verify emulated tool calls emit the same SSE frames (`tool_call`, confirmation flow) as native ones — the confirmation-required tools (`core:write/edit/shell`) must still pause for approval.

### How to verify done

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] With `deepseek-r1:14b` selected, the toolkit selector is visible; selecting the `core` toolkit and asking the model to read a file executes the tool and the answer uses the file's content.
- [ ] A multi-step tool chain (≥2 sequential calls) completes on an emulated model.
- [ ] Confirmation-required tools (`core:shell`) still pause the stream and wait for user approval in emulated mode.
- [ ] An unlisted non-tool model (no JSON entry) no longer produces a raw error — it falls back to emulation automatically.
- [ ] A native tool-capable Ollama model (e.g. `qwen3`) is unchanged: still uses native `tools`, zero behavior diff.
- [ ] Malformed model output (broken JSON) degrades to a normal text reply — never a crash or hung stream.
- [ ] `npm test` passes; new unchain parser unit tests pass.
- [ ] Manual smoke via the dev test API (`docs/api-reference/test-api.md`): send a tool-requiring message on an emulated model and assert the tool-call frame appears in the trace.

### Impact / risk

**HIGH — treat with care:**

- `OllamaModelIO.fetch_turn` is the **single driver for all Ollama chats** — every Ollama conversation, tool-using or not, flows through your changes. A regression here breaks all local-model chat. Keep the native path byte-identical when `supports_tools` is true.
- `chat.js` gating logic sits on the main chat page; the forced-empty-toolkits behavior interacts with session state (`session.selectedToolkits` is preserved by design — keep that).

**MEDIUM:**

- Emulation quality is inherently model-dependent: small models produce malformed JSON often. The parser's failure mode must always be "graceful plain-text turn", never a stuck stream.
- Capability-shape change (`/models/catalog`) touches a documented data contract — update `docs/data-models/model-and-toolkit-catalog.md` in the same PR.

title: Git toolkit
body:
# GitToolkit v1：本地 Git 安全封装

## Summary
- 新增 builtin `git` toolkit，第一版只覆盖本地 Git 工作流，不做 GitHub PR/issue/API。
- 保留 `ExternalAPIToolkit` 里的旧 git 工具以避免破坏兼容性；新 `GitToolkit` 使用同名安全工具，文档标明不要和 `external_api` 同时加载。
- 安全原则：不接受任意 git args、不走 shell、所有路径限制在 workspace/repo 内，修改 index/history 的工具必须走 confirmation。

## Key Changes
- 新增 `GitToolkit(workspace_root=None, workspace_roots=None)`，注册这些工具：
  - `git_status(cwd=".", include_untracked=True, max_output_chars=20000)`
  - `git_diff(cwd=".", staged=False, paths=None, context_lines=3, max_output_chars=50000)`
  - `git_stage(paths, cwd=".", max_output_chars=20000)`
  - `git_unstage(paths, cwd=".", max_output_chars=20000)`
  - `git_commit(message, cwd=".", max_output_chars=20000)`
- `git_status` / `git_diff` 不需要确认；`git_stage` / `git_unstage` / `git_commit` 需要确认。
- `git_commit` 只提交已 staged 的内容，不自动 stage，不接受额外 args，不跳过 hooks；没有 staged changes 时直接返回错误。
- `git_commit` 的 confirmation resolver 生成 staged diff 预览，`interact_type="code_diff"`；diff 无法生成或过大时退回普通确认。
- 所有工具返回统一结构：`ok`, `action`, `cwd`, `repo_root`, `argv`, `returncode`, `stdout`, `stderr`, `timed_out`, `truncated`，并在 status/diff 中附带结构化 file summary。
- 新增 builtin manifest `id = "git"`、轻量 README，并导出 `GitToolkit`；registry 测试更新为包含 `core`、`external_api`、`git`。

## Implementation Notes
- 新建 `src/unchain/toolkits/builtin/git/`，复用 `BuiltinToolkit` 的 workspace root 校验。
- Git 命令统一通过 `subprocess.run(..., shell=False)` 执行，并使用固定 argv 模板：
  - status: `git status --short --branch --untracked-files=all`
  - diff: `git diff --no-ext-diff --unified=<n> [--cached] -- <paths>`
  - stage: `git add -- <paths>`
  - unstage: `git restore --staged -- <paths>`
  - commit: `git commit -m <message>`
- `cwd` 必须在 workspace roots 内；执行前用 `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` 找 repo root，并拒绝 repo root 不在 workspace roots 内的调用。
- `paths` 必须是非空 list，逐项解析后必须仍在 repo root 内；不支持 `"."`、glob 展开、`--` 参数注入或 pathspec magic。
- 实施代码修改前按项目规则对将编辑的 symbol 跑 GitNexus impact；提交前跑 GitNexus detect_changes。

## Test Plan
- 新增 `tests/test_git_toolkit.py`，用 `tmp_path` 初始化 git repo，并配置本地 `user.name` / `user.email`。
- 覆盖 status/diff：非 repo、clean repo、modified file、staged diff、path filter、输出截断。
- 覆盖安全限制：cwd 越界、path 越界、空 paths、伪造 `--flag` path、无 git executable 或 git 返回非零。
- 覆盖 mutating tools：stage 后 status 变化、unstage 后恢复、commit 只提交 staged 内容、无 staged changes 失败。
- 覆盖 confirmation：`git_commit` resolver 返回 staged code diff；diff 不可用时退回普通 confirmation。
- 更新 registry/export 测试，确认 builtin toolkit 列表和 tool count 正确。

## Assumptions
- 第一版 toolkit 名称采用 `GitToolkit` / manifest id `git`，不是 `GitHubToolkit`。
- 第一版不包含 `push`、`pull`、`branch`、`checkout`、`merge`、`reset`、`stash`、PR 或 issue 操作。
- 旧 `ExternalAPIToolkit` 的 git 工具暂时保留，后续单独做 deprecation/migration。

## Changes

## Problem

When a new version of PuPu is released, the download links in `README.md` on the `main` branch still point to the old version's assets. For example, the current latest release is **v0.1.4** with assets:
- `PuPu-0.1.4-arm64.dmg`
- `PuPu.Setup.0.1.4.exe`
- `PuPu_0.1.4.deb`

But the README still has hardcoded **0.1.3** in all download URLs and filenames:
- `https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/latest/download/PuPu.Setup.0.1.3.exe`
- `https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/latest/download/PuPu-0.1.3-arm64.dmg`

- `https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/PuPu/releases/latest/download/PuPu_0.1.3.deb`
- `sudo apt install ./PuPu_0.1.3.deb` (in the code block)

## Solution

Create a new GitHub Actions workflow at `.github/workflows/update-readme-download-links.yml` that:

1. **Triggers** on `release` event with type `published`.
2. **Extracts** the new version number from the release tag (e.g., `v0.1.4` → `0.1.4`).
3. **Fetches** the list of actual release asset filenames from the GitHub API for that release.
4. **Scans** `README.md` for all download URLs that point to `releases/latest/download/` and also any version strings in inline code/commands (like `sudo apt install ./PuPu_X.Y.Z.deb`).
5. **Checks** whether the filenames in those README links match the actual release assets.
6. **If mismatched**, automatically updates the README by replacing old version strings in download links and commands with the new version number.
7. **Creates a PR** targeting `main` branch with the updated README, titled something like `docs: update README download links to vX.Y.Z`.

- The workflow should use `peter-evans/create-pull-request` or a similar well-known action to create the PR.
- The PR branch name should be something like `auto/update-readme-downloads-vX.Y.Z`.

- The version replacement should handle all patterns found in the current README:

Any PR targeting `main` from a branch other than `dev` should fail CI, blocking the merge.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/enforce-merge-source.yml`** — new workflow that triggers on PRs targeting `main`, checks `github.head_ref == "dev"`, and exits 1 if not
  - Scoped to `permissions: contents: read` (least-privilege)

```yaml
- name: Check if source branch is dev
  run: |
    if [ "${{ github.head_ref }}" != "dev" ]; then
      echo "❌ Only the 'dev' branch is allowed to merge into 'main'."
      exit 1
    else
      echo "✅ Source branch is 'dev'. Merge allowed."
    fi
```

## Required follow-up

Add `check-source-branch` as a **required status check** on the `main` branch ruleset — without this, the failing check won't block merges.

- **`use_chat_input_models.js`** — Initializes `collapsedGroups` so all groups start collapsed except the one containing the currently selected model. Uses `Object.values(MODEL_GROUPS)` to stay forward-compatible with new groups.

  ```js

    const activeGroup = get_group_of_model(selectedModelId);
    return Object.fromEntries(
      Object.values(MODEL_GROUPS).map((g) => [g, g !== activeGroup]),
  ```

title: Add Generic Model Support Capability to PuPu and Document Integration Workflow
body:
# Feature Request: Add Generic Model Support for PuPu and Document Integration Workflow

This ticket proposes to enhance the PuPu desktop client by enabling support for new AI models, and to document the general process for model integration. It is *not limited* to any specific model, aiming to make the workflow repeatable for future additions.

## Workflow for Adding a New Model

1. **Navigate to the Miso Project's `miso` Folder**
   - Open the `miso` project and locate the `miso` directory.

2. **Review and Update the Model Management JSON Files**
   - In the `miso` folder, identify the following two model management files:
     - [`model_capabilities.json`](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/miso/blob/main/miso/model_capabilities.json): Defines supported models and their capabilities (e.g., provider, context window, support for tools, reasoning, modalities, and allowed payload keys).
     - [`model_default_payloads.json`](https://github.com/haoxiang-xu/miso/blob/main/miso/model_default_payloads.json): Defines default parameters for each model when invoked (e.g., temperature, max_output_tokens, truncation, reasoning, etc.).
   - To add a new model:
     - In `model_capabilities.json`, following the existing structure, add a new model entry specifying its capabilities and payload keys.
     - In `model_default_payloads.json`, specify the default request parameters for the new model - refer to other models for the required key set and value types.

3. **Save Changes and Restart PuPu Client**
   - After updating both JSON files, save your changes and restart the PuPu desktop client to reload the model configuration.

4. **Test Model Functionalities**
   - After PuPu restarts and loads the new model, test all capabilities declared in `model_capabilities.json` for the model to ensure that each can be utilized fully.
   - If any capability fails, trace the issue and repeat the above steps after corrections.

## Notes
- This process can be repeated for any future models you wish to add.
- If incompatibilities or feature gaps are encountered, document them for follow-up or possible platform enhancements.

__Suggested labels__: `new feature`, `model`

title: In narrow-screen mode, the `chat message list` is wider than the `input textfield`, which makes the UI look unbalanced.
Update LLM_endpoint for REST-based provider support
Add Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini REST providers with tool calling support
body:
Extends `LLM_endpoint` to support Anthropic Claude (`claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022`) and Google Gemini (`gemini-1.5-flash`) via their REST APIs, with full tool calling integration using the existing `LLM_toolkit` schema.

## Changes

- **Fixed mutable default arguments** in `LLM_tool.__init__`, `LLM_toolkit.__init__`, and `LLM_endpoint.chat_completion` (changed `[]`/`{}` to `None` with proper initialization)

- **Added API key parameters** `claude_api_key` and `gemini_api_key` to `LLM_endpoint.__init__`

- **Implemented Anthropic provider** (`anthropic_fetch_response`)
  - Converts messages/tools to Anthropic Messages API format (`input_schema`)
  - Handles streaming SSE responses with `content_block_delta` events
  - Executes tool calls via `LLM_toolkit.execute` and appends results to message flow
  - 300s timeout, proper JSON parsing error handling

- **Implemented Gemini provider** (`gemini_fetch_response`)
  - Converts messages/tools to Gemini format (`functionDeclarations`)
  - Handles streaming SSE responses with `functionCall` parts
  - Executes function calls via `LLM_toolkit.execute` and appends results to message flow
  - 300s timeout, proper error handling

- **Updated provider routing** to use `elif` chain supporting `"anthropic"` and `"gemini"` alongside existing `"openai"` and `"ollama"`

## Usage

```python
# Anthropic Claude
endpoint = LLM_endpoint(
    claude_api_key="sk-ant-...",
    provider="anthropic",
    model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022"
)
endpoint.toolkit = LLM_toolkit(tools={"calculator": calc_tool})
response = endpoint.chat_completion(messages, callback=stream_handler)

# Google Gemini  
endpoint = LLM_endpoint(
    gemini_api_key="AIza...",
    provider="gemini",
    model="gemini-1.5-flash"
)
endpoint.toolkit = LLM_toolkit(tools={"search": search_tool})
response = endpoint.chat_completion(messages)
```

Tool execution flow matches existing OpenAI/Ollama behavior: LLM requests tool → `toolkit.execute(name, args)` → result appended to message history → returned.

Migrate from localStorage to Electron file-based storage
body:
Replaces browser localStorage with Electron main process file storage under `userData/storage/`. No migration of existing data.

## Storage Layout

```
userData/storage/
├── address_book.json          # Chat sessions metadata
├── favoured_models.json       # User model preferences
├── sections/<address>.json    # Chat history per session
└── files/<key>.txt            # Uploaded images (base64)
```

- Added IPC handlers for CRUD operations on JSON files

- Separate handlers for sections, files, and metadata

**Preload bridge** (`public/preload.js`)
- Exposed `storageAPI` via contextBridge for renderer access

**Storage abstraction** (`src/utils/storage.js`)
- New module wrapping IPC calls with error handling
- Async API matching file operations

- Converted all localStorage calls to async storage API

- File operations (`save_input_files`, `load_saved_files`) properly awaited

**Storage UI** (`src/COMPONENTs/settings/storage_manager/storage_manager.js`)
- Updated size calculation to query filesystem via IPC
- Delete operations now remove both section JSON and associated files

**Chat component** (`src/COMPONENTs/chat/chat.js`)
- `on_input_submit` and `update_message` made async to await file saves/loads
- Message component loads files asynchronously

```javascript
localStorage.setItem(UNIQUE_KEY + "address_book", JSON.stringify(data));
const data = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(UNIQUE_KEY + "address_book"));
```
